children: Before exposing the crooked framework of Roman denialism, I will present five episodes or texts that span the period from the fifth to the thirteenth century and illustrate how Byzantines used the ethnonym Roman, especially in contexts that juxtaposed Romans with others. Who used it? With reference to whom? And what were the criteria that justified its use? What made someone a Roman in Byzantium? In a previous monograph I examined the political dimension of this problem, arguing that the Byzantines were Romans because they were members of a specific polity that derived its origins and distinctive political ideology from ancient Rome.

This book will add an ethnic dimension to that definition: the Byzantine Romans were also an ethnic group. This proposal is far removed from the picture presented by many Byzantinists, but it emerges with striking clarity and forcefulness from the sources. The following texts were chosen to highlight the ethnic aspects of Romanness in Byzantium. They are not eccentric, but they do reveal more explicitly what is taken for granted in other sources, and there are more like them that I could have chosen. I present them here, before the exposé of the field’s habits of denial, to show what kind of evidence Byzantinists have to circumvent in order to continue to deny that the Byzantines were Romans.

en: Why was everyone so concerned to have a proper Roman emperor and prevent foreign elements from occupying the throne? The deceased emperor Zeno (474–491), whose body lay in state in the palace while this exchange was taking place, was an Isaurian from southern Asia Minor. The Isaurians are stereotypically described in Roman sources as mostly uncivilized mountain dwellers. They made good soldiers, but were perceived by many as violent, greedy, and insufficiently Romanized. Even though they were Roman citizens like everyone else in the empire, “Isaurians and Romans” could be juxtaposed as different categories, and the former could be labeled an
(people, ethnic group, or nation).
In 468, the emperor Leo issued a law against private persons keeping armed slaves, private armies, and their own Isaurians.
In 473, there was a massacre of Isaurians in Constantinople when an incident in the hippodrome sparked violence.
Zeno’s background was a liability. A contemporary Syriac chronicle states bluntly that palace officials hated him “because he was an Isaurian by birth.”

His native name was Tarasis Kodissa, which he changed to get ahead in imperial politics. The people of Constantinople at first refused to make him a partner in imperial power at the request of the emperor Leo, and he came to power indirectly, as the guardian of his son, Leo’s grandson, Leo II, who died prematurely. Within a year of his accession, Zeno was temporarily deposed by rivals while Constantinople erupted in another massacre of Isaurians.
These pogroms suggest that people believed that they could tell who was an Isaurian, indicating that they were regarded as a distinct ethnic group.

children: The person eventually elected in 491 was Anastasios (491–518), a native of the city of Dyrrachion (classical Epidamnos) on the Adriatic coast. Presumably, nothing about his origins seemed ethnically foreign or posed an obstacle. Still, within a few years of his election, if not immediately, Anastasios put it about that he was a descendant of Pompey the Great, as the name ran in his family.

Thus, to prove his Romanness, Anastasios claimed to be biologically descended from a general of the Republic. He also expelled leading Isaurians from Constantinople and launched a full-scale imperial war against their homeland, pacifying it once and for all.

Konstantinos VII Porphyrogennetos’ zoology of nations

. In the midtenth century, the emperor Konstantinos VII assembled a text whose purpose was to instruct his son and heir Romanos II how to deal with the foreign nations that surrounded the Romans. Chapter 13 of this text gives advice on how to cleverly and even deceitfully turn away foreign demands for imperial vestments, Greek fire, and royal brides. The basic excuse—a lie—is that an angel of God instructed Constantine the Great to place a curse on the altar of Hagia Sophia against giving any of those things away: “Never shall an emperor of the Romans ally himself in marriage with a nation whose customs differ from and are alien to those of the Roman order, especially with one that is infidel and unbaptized, unless it be with the Franks alone.”

At this point Konstantinos counters the objection that his predecessor and father-in-law Romanos I Lakapenos had in fact made a marriage alliance with the Bulgarian tsar. His argument is that Romanos I was a man of humble origins who did not properly understand the customs of the Roman court. Konstantinos concedes that Romanos may have countered that the Bulgarians were Orthodox Christians “just like us” (i.e., us Romans), but this response does not pass muster with Konstantinos, who cannot overlook “this innovation in the polity of the Romans.”

It goes beyond the idea of the nation as a community of values and postulates biological kinship as its foundation. Konstantinos even compares the nations of the world to different animal species. His logic defines the Romans as one nation

among others. Konstantinos does not say that they are qualitatively different or better than others, though presumably he did believe it. He defines nations by customs, laws, institutions, language, and intermarriage, which makes each nation also into a “race” or “tribe” (

en: Konstantinos’ concept is equivalent to standard modern definitions of the nation.
Byzantinists are disingenuous when they say that the Byzantines would have been “surprised” to hear themselves described as a Roman nation.

As we will see, they consistently claimed to be precisely that. Instead, they would have been surprised by the modern error that “Roman” was somehow a multiethnic category. This modern idea would have sounded to them like a contradiction in terms, as for them Romans and foreign ethnics were separate categories.

我们将会看到，他们一贯声称自己恰恰就是如此。相反，让他们惊讶的会是现代人的错误观念，即“罗马人”不知怎的是一个多族群类别。这种现代观念在他们听来会像是用词矛盾，因为在他们那里，罗马人与外族是彼此分离的类别。

Language is now promoted as a chief distinguishing trait. But the modern ecumenical reading of Byzantine Orthodoxy as somehow transcending ethnicity is misleading too. By the middle period, the Church prohibited marriages between Orthodox and non-Orthodox, on the grounds that “one must not mix things that are discrete.”

The latter over time came to include many of the empire’s neighbors, such as the Armenians and even the Latins. Thus the rules of the Church regarding marriage tended to partially reinforce the kinship basis of the Roman community.
zh: 君士坦丁的说法还与另一种现代预期不符，后人以为拜占庭人会把宗教当作界定自身的特征。他没有特别提出正教信仰，大概是因为这样会动摇他对保加利亚人与罗马人的区分。罗曼努斯一世·拉卡佩努斯把孙女嫁给了保加利亚人，对方也是正教基督徒。这样，君士坦丁就打破了我们在《圣德米特里奥斯圣迹集》中看到的
（genos）与宗教之间的纽带。语言成为主要的区分特征之一。然而，今日对拜占庭正教作普世主义的解读，仿佛它凌驾于族群性之上，同样会误导人。到拜占庭中期，教会已禁止正教信徒与非正教信徒通婚，理由是“彼此有别之物不可混杂”。
随着时间推移，后者包括了许多帝国的邻人，比如亚美尼亚人，甚至拉丁人。因此，教会的婚姻规定往往在一定程度上巩固了罗马共同体的亲属关系基础。

children: Overall, it appears that the Romans defined themselves as a nation through a constellation of customs, traits, and practices (including religion) and by a shared homeland or geographical location. At each time, they highlighted the elements that worked best to distinguish them from other nations given the circumstances. Sometimes it was their religion, sometimes their language, and sometimes it could even be their hats.
The emperor Andronikos I Komnenos’ plan to kill all his enemies

. As Andronikos I (1183–1185) was growing unpopular and the polity was speaking out against him, he convened a council of state where he proposed to execute his political enemies “along with all who are related to them by blood.” His son Manuel opposed this, arguing that the decree, if literally enforced, would lead to the death of the entire Roman population—τὸ Πανρώμαιον—and not only of all the Romans but of some foreigners too. Specifically, he argued that the family of each of the accused extended from one relation to the next, through biological relatives and in-laws, in a long chain of affiliation such that eventually all the Romans would have to be killed, and the number of victims would be “infinite” (ἄπειρον). This was hyperbole, but his reasoning reveals that the totality of the Romans (what he calls the
) was for him not a small group but rather a national or ethnic community defined by
and constituted mostly through kinship. As some Romans were married to “ethnic types” (ἐξ ἔθνους), quite a few of the latter would perish too.
Manuel would know this, as he was married to a Georgian princess.
Ethnic enclaves in the thirteenth-century Balkans

. In 1246, the town of Melnik was contested between the emperor of the Romans at Nikaia and the Bulgarian tsar. The majority of the population, however, were ethnic Romans. The historian of the Nikaian empire, Georgios Akropolites, makes their leading citizen deliver a speech to the rest, reminding them that “the emperor of the Romans has rights over us, seeing as our territory belongs to the empire of the Romans . . . moreover, we all originate in Philippopolis [they had been resettled in Melnik by a previous tsar] and we are pure Romans when it comes to our
The concept of a “pure Roman” is striking. Conversely, Akropolites admits that Bulgarians living under the Roman empire of Nikaia naturally “wanted to side with people of the same race as themselves
and cast off the yoke of those who spoke a separate language
”—the Romans—“for whom they harbored a deep hatred.”

Ethnicity in these cases was not decided by imperial affiliation but by cultural traits such as language, historical memory, and perceptions of ethnic kinship. The Nikaian Roman historian did not try to paint every subject of his emperor as a loyal Roman; instead, he revealed that states and ethnicities did not perfectly line up in those chaotic times.

The most straightforward conclusion to draw from these testimonies is that the Romans of Byzantium saw themselves as an ethnic group or nation, defined in the same way that ethnic groups and nations are understood by modern scholars and sociologists: they had their own ethnonym, language, customs, laws and institutions, homeland, and sense (even if imagined) that they were related by kinship and taxonomically different from other ethnic groups. These testimonies come from many centuries that span the long history of the empire’s existence; they reflect the voices of provincials and Constantinopolitans alike and are taken from different genres of evidence. Even if we want to hold off momentarily on the specific conclusion that the Romans of Byzantium were an ethnicity or nation, these five moments still give us prima facie reason to believe that they were Romans in some deeper sense than the merely formal one of belonging to an empire that called itself, at the top, “the empire of the Romans.” We can certainly say that most Byzantines had something to do with being Roman. It does appear difficult to deny this.
总的来说，罗马人似乎凭借一组共同的习俗、特征和做法（包括宗教），以及共同的故土或地理位置，把自己界定为一个民族。在不同时期，他们会凸显当时最能将自己与其他民族区别开来的要素，有时是宗教，有时是语言，有时甚至是帽子。
安德罗尼库斯一世·科穆宁皇帝计划杀尽仇敌。

安德罗尼库斯一世（1183–1185年在位）日益不得人心，政治共同体中反对他的声音越来越多。他召集了一次国务会议，提议处死政敌，“连同一切与他们有血缘关系的人”。其子曼努埃尔反对，说这道法令若照字面执行，就会害死整个罗马人口（τὸ Πανρώμαιον），甚至还会害死一些外人。他指出，每个被指控者的家族都能由一个亲属顺延到另一个亲属，血亲与姻亲相连，牵出一长串关系。到头来所有罗马人都得被杀，遇害者将“数也数不尽”（ἄπειρον）。这固然夸张，但其推理表明，所谓全体罗马人（
（genos）界定、主要由亲属关系联结起来的一个民族或族群共同体，人数众多。因为有些罗马人与“异族”（ἐξ ἔθνους）通婚，外人也会有不少丧生。
曼努埃尔当然知道这一点，他娶的是一位格鲁吉亚公主。
十三世纪巴尔干的族群飞地。
1246年，梅尔尼克镇是尼西亚的罗马人皇帝和保加利亚沙皇争夺的地方。然而当地居民大多是族群意义上的罗马人。尼西亚帝国的史家乔治·阿克罗波利特斯在记述中让当地为首的一位市民对众人发表演说，提醒大家：“罗马人的皇帝对我们有管辖权，因为我们的土地属于罗马人的帝国……况且，我们都来自菲利波波利斯［早先有一位沙皇把他们迁到梅尔尼克］，就
（genos）而言，我们是纯正的罗马人（καθαροὶ τὸ γένος Ῥωμαῖοι）。”
“纯正的罗马人”这个观念引人注目。反过来，阿克罗波利特斯也承认，尼西亚罗马帝国治下的保加利亚人自然“愿意站在自己
（alloglossoi）的人”，也就是罗马人，“给他们加上的枷锁，他们对那些人深恶痛绝”。
在这些事例中，决定族群性的不是隶属哪个帝国，而是语言、历史记忆和对族群亲缘的认识等文化特征。这位尼西亚的罗马史家没有试图把皇帝手下的所有臣民都写成忠心的罗马人，他反而让人看到，在那动荡的时代，国家与族群并不完全重合。

从这些证据最直接可得的结论是，拜占庭的罗马人认为自己是一个族群或民族，与现代学者和社会学家对族群和民族的理解相合。他们有自己的族名、语言、习俗、法律和制度、故土，也认为彼此有亲缘关系（即使这种关系出于想象），在分类上与其他族群有别。这些材料来自帝国漫长历史中的不同时期，包括行省居民和君士坦丁堡人的声音，分属不同史料体裁。即使暂时搁置拜占庭的罗马人是一个族群或民族这一具体结论，这五个事例也给出了初步理由，让我们相信他们是在某种更深的意义上成为罗马人的，远不止在形式上隶属一个由最高层称为“罗马人的帝国”的国家。可以肯定的是，大多数拜占庭人确实与罗马人身份有某种关联。看来，这很难否认。

en: Yet denial is precisely what a dominant strain within Byzantine Studies has long advocated, developing strategies for refusing to accept the obvious. One strategy is suppression, or just looking the other way. The testimonies presented above, along with many others like them, are rarely discussed, mentioned, or even cited in most works of Byzantine scholarship that purport to be studies of identity. The issue of Roman identity is instead often transposed to a religious or even metaphysical level, where we find much talk of God crowning the emperor, something called the
and End-Time fantasy. These denialist acrobatics operate at such a high level of abstraction that the
or

of the Romans is obscured from sight. The Byzantines’ claim to be Romans has also been branded an act of deception. We now have “critical” studies that argue that all this Roman business was nothing more than a literary game played by a small elite in Constantinople. Such research draws its conclusions without offering close readings of actual discursive claims to Roman identity made in the sources, such as were surveyed above.

It does not so much brush them aside as pretend that they do not exist. As it cannot offer any positive evidence in favor of its thesis, it relies instead on the existing predisposition to doubt that the Byzantines were “really” Romans. The sources are full of claims to what can only be called a Roman ethnicity, but modern scholarship on Byzantium suppresses them or denies their significance.
zh: 然而，否认恰恰是拜占庭研究一股主流思潮长期以来奉行的做法。为了拒绝接受明摆着的事实，它发展出各种策略，其中一种是压下相关证据，或干脆视而不见。上述证据以及许多类似材料，在大多数自称研究认同的拜占庭学著作中，很少得到讨论、提及，甚至很少被引用。罗马认同问题反倒常被移到宗教、乃至形而上学的层面。人们大谈上帝为皇帝加冕、大谈所谓的
（oecumene 或 ecumene）和末世幻想。这些否认论的花招过于抽象，遮蔽了罗马人的
（genos）或
（ethnos）。拜占庭人自称罗马人，也被指为欺骗。如今已有“批判性”研究声称，这一切关于罗马人的说法不过是君士坦丁堡少数精英在玩文字游戏。这类研究没有细读史料中实际表达的罗马认同，包括上文所考察的那些说法，便下了结论。
与其说它们撇开了这一类材料，不如说它们假装这些材料并不存在。它们拿不出任何可以正面支持自身论点的证据，就倚赖学界早有的倾向，怀疑拜占庭人是否“真的”是罗马人。史料里有大量这样的自我表述，只能称为罗马族群性的表述，现代拜占庭研究却将它们压下去，或否认其意义。

en: What is going on?
zh: 这是怎么回事？

en: A Thousand Years of Denial
zh: 千年的否认

en: Before the mid-eighth century, the Latin west casually accepted what we call Byzantium as the empire of the Romans, or the
There were lingering traces of Latin bias against the eastern “Greeks,” but at this time they were marginal.
This changed during the second half of the eighth century, when the popes pivoted and sought to replace the patronage of Constantinople with that of the Franks. At this point, the term
began to displace
in western references to the eastern empire.

This intensified when some Frankish kings began, if at first only sporadically and uncertainly, to claim for themselves the title of emperor of the Romans. By the ninth century, both popes and western emperors were, in their official correspondence, actively questioning the right of the eastern emperor to call himself emperor of the Romans.

As papal and imperial German ambitions began to draw more heavily on Rome’s prestige, hegemonic apparatus, and language of power, they saw eastern claims to them as an obstacle. Above and beyond their mutual rivalry, the popes and German emperors had a common interest to exclude Constantinople’s claims to the Roman tradition. Thus, the easterners were increasingly reclassified as

a term that in ancient Latin literature conveyed negative connotations that were now reactivated, connotations of treachery, effeminacy, excessive sophistication, love of luxury, verbal trickery, and cowardice.
To avoid calling the emperor of the Romans by his true title, western authors invented a number of alternatives, such as
and
Those would remain the dominant terms in the west until the nineteenth century, at which point they were replaced by
(see below). Naturally, the eastern Romans disliked being called Greeks. One emperor even threw papal emissaries into prison for bearing letters that addressed him as such.
zh: 八世纪中叶以前，拉丁西方并不质疑我们所谓的拜占庭就是罗马人的帝国，即“罗马国家”（
）。拉丁人对东方“希腊人”的偏见仍留有痕迹，但当时并不显著。
八世纪下半叶，教皇转而寻求法兰克人的庇护，以取代君士坦丁堡的庇护，情形就此改变。西方在称呼东部帝国时，开始用“
”（Graeci）取代“
”（Romani）。
随后，一些法兰克国王也开始自称罗马人的皇帝。尽管最初只偶尔这样自称，态度也不确定，这一趋势却因此加剧。到九世纪，教皇与西方皇帝已在官方通信中主动质疑东部皇帝自称罗马人的皇帝的权利。
教皇与德意志皇帝的抱负越来越仰赖罗马的声望、称霸所凭借的制度及其权力用语，便把东部对这些遗产的主张视为障碍。两者虽相互竞争，却都希望排斥君士坦丁堡对罗马传统的主张。于是，东方人越来越常被重新归为“
”（Graeci）。这个词在古代拉丁文学中的贬义重新流行，意指背信弃义、女性化、过分工于世故、爱好奢华、能言善骗和懦弱。
为了避免用罗马人的皇帝的真实头衔称呼他，西方作者造出几种替代用语，例如“
”。西方直到十九世纪都主要采用这些称呼，后来才改用“
”（见下文）。东部罗马人当然不喜欢被叫作希腊人。有一位皇帝甚至把教皇使节关进监狱，就因为他们送来的信这样称呼他。

en: The issue was not merely one of east-west rivalry over the titles and the prestige of Rome. Independently of the eastern claim, in the emerging cultural world of Latin-Catholic Europe the memory of Rome had become a paradigm and common reference point by which diverse polities, peoples, languages, and churches were coordinated.

Beyond the imperial projects of popes and German kings, the idea of Rome was one of the few things holding the west together, to the degree that it had any common identity. The east, however, was excluded from this club, as its engagement with Rome was configured in vastly different ways than the ideas evolving in the west, so differently that it could not interface with the ongoing western reception of Rome. Eventually, it made no intuitive sense in the west to think of the eastern empire as a shareholder in the Roman tradition, and these intuitive axioms were carried forward and entrenched in scholarship. The process was neither instantaneous nor universal. There were always Latins who recognized the eastern empire as Roman and its people as Romans. But over time their numbers thinned, and the crusades intensified the anti-Greek bias. Cut off by language, the Byzantines were unable to participate or keep up with Latin intellectual developments, including the cultivation of Roman law, while their Church was increasingly perceived as deviating from the standards of the Church of Rome. An element of charged sexual polemic further cast the
as unworthy candidates for the legacy of Rome,

and the conquest of Constantinople in 1204 and subsequent dismemberment of their empire made the previously rhetorical humiliations real. The sack of Constantinople was regarded by some in the west as payback for the sack of Troy: the Franks, related to the ancient Romans via a Trojan genealogy, were getting back at those perfidious Greeks.
zh: 问题并不限于东西双方争夺罗马的头衔和声望。无论东部如何主张，在逐渐成形的拉丁天主教欧洲文化世界里，罗马的记忆已成为一种范式和共同参照，不同的政治共同体、人民、语言和教会据此相互联结。

除了教皇和德意志国王的帝国计划，罗马观念也是少数将西方维系在一起的事物之一，西方倘有什么共同认同，也基于此。然而东部被排除在外，因为它同罗马的关系与西方逐渐发展的观念相去甚远，无法同西方当时接受罗马传统的方式接轨。到了后来，西方人凭直觉已无法把东部帝国看作罗马传统的共同继承者。这些被视作理所当然的看法一路传入学界，并在那里根深蒂固。这一过程并非一蹴即就，也并未波及所有人。始终有拉丁人承认东部帝国是罗马的，其人民是罗马人。但持此观点的人日渐稀少，十字军东征又加重了反希腊的偏见。受语言阻隔，拜占庭人无法参与或跟上拉丁世界思想的发展，包括对罗马法的研习，而他们的教会也愈发被认为偏离了罗马教会的规范。充满敌意的性别与性方面的论战，进一步把“
”说成不配继承罗马遗产。
1204年君士坦丁堡被攻占，其后帝国四分五裂，此前限于言辞的羞辱化为现实。西方有些人把洗劫君士坦丁堡看成对洗劫特洛伊的报复：法兰克人凭特洛伊族谱与古罗马人相认，如今终于能报复那些背信弃义的希腊人。

en: To make a long story short, western medieval observers and polemicists constructed an image of Byzantium that functioned as a discourse of orientalism parallel to that directed against the Muslim east. It was a package of distortions and strategic misunderstandings that stripped Byzantium of its claim to Rome and eventually also justified its conquest, exploitation, and (failed) attempts at conversion by western powers. This image continued without interruption down to the nineteenth century, when the field of Byzantine Studies came into being, even though it had evolved in the meantime. This is not the place to tell that story in detail. Suffice it to say that, to a considerable degree, that field was at first a systematization of preexisting prejudices: biases with references.
zh: 长话短说，西方中世纪的观察家与论战家构建了一个拜占庭形象，其功能是与针对穆斯林东方的那种话语平行的东方主义话语。这是一套扭曲与策略性误解的组合，它剥夺了拜占庭对罗马的主张，并最终为西方列强对它的征服、剥削和（失败的）改宗企图提供了正当性。这一形象不间断地延续到十九世纪拜占庭研究学科诞生之时，尽管其间它已有所演变。这里不是详述那段故事的地方。只需说，在很大程度上，该学科起初是对既有偏见的系统化：带参考文献的偏见。

en: The polemic against the medieval “Greeks” had, in the meantime, been intensified by the thinkers of the Enlightenment. Montesquieu and Gibbon cast the “empire of the Greeks” as a steady decline from the peak of ancient Rome. Yet it is fascinating that “on the odd occasion when in his opinion “the Greeks” get something right (such as winning a battle), Gibbon will consider reverting to ‘Romans.’”

Otherwise, in Enlightenment thought Byzantium became a symbol for all that could potentially still go wrong in Europe’s triple inheritance from antiquity: Byzantium was populated by degenerate Greeks, whose language had declined; it was a corrupt New Rome, run by scheming eunuchs and women; and it was retarded by a superstitious form of Christianity that was addicted to icons and hair-splitting theology. Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau, Hegel, and many others indulged in cringeworthy comments about this extinct medieval civilization, which they deployed strategically as an archetypal antithesis of the enlightened state and society that they hoped to see emerge in the west. Perhaps this imaginary Byzantium of the philosophers was not supposed to be historical at all: it functioned as a screen on which they could safely project all that they feared and disliked about their own world and its pitfalls, a dystopian mirror for the early modern nation-state.
zh: 其间，启蒙思想家使针对中世纪“希腊人”的论战愈演愈烈。孟德斯鸠和吉本把“希腊人的帝国”写成古罗马登峰之后的一路衰落。但有趣的是，“偶尔在他看来，‘希腊人’做对了一件事（比如打赢一场战役），吉本便会考虑改回‘罗马人’的称呼”。

除此之外，启蒙思想把拜占庭当作欧洲从古代继承的三重遗产可能遭遇的一切不幸的象征：拜占庭住着一群退化的希腊人，连语言也衰落了；它是腐败的新罗马，由善于耍阴谋的宦官和女人把持；一种迷信的基督教让它停滞不前，这种基督教耽于圣像和烦琐的神学争辩。孟德斯鸠、伏尔泰、卢梭、黑格尔以及许多其他人，纵情发表过不少令人难堪的评论，有意把这个已消亡的中世纪文明当作典型的反例，与他们希望在西方看到的开明国家和社会对照。哲学家想象中的这个拜占庭，也许根本无需符合历史。这个虚构的对象让他们可以放心地将对自己所处世界及其凶险的一切恐惧和厌恶投射上去，仿佛一面照出近代早期民族国家噩梦的镜子。

en: Be that as it may, this strategy pushed a historical civilization deeper into the mud of western polemic. The Enlightenment created an even more negative ideological crucible for the study of Byzantium in western scholarship, which effectively perpetuated medieval biases. Byzantium was still intuitively seen in terms of its Greek ethnicity and deviant faith (which we call Orthodoxy), and there was little esteem for either. The idea that the Byzantines might legitimately be Romans, not just in an abstract sense of titular continuity but as an ethnicity, appears preposterous under this light. The Byzantines spoke Greek, did not rule in Rome, and were not Roman Catholics. Thus, they had nothing to do with Rome in terms of language (and so ethnicity), geography, or religion. This view has become for many a form of “mental wallpaper,”
the “most hardwired instincts [that] have usually been left out of the spotlight of inquiry.”

But sometimes the most obvious and natural positions are the most ideological. They require otherwise sensible historians to get into impossible contortions in order to deny the Romanness of the Byzantines, all because they accept “intuitive” premises over the plain evidence of the sources.
zh: 不管怎样，这一策略把一个真实存在过的文明推入了西方论战的更深处。启蒙运动把西方学界对拜占庭的研究放进了一个更为负面的意识形态环境，实际上延续了中世纪的偏见。当时人们仍习惯从希腊族群身份和背离正道的信仰这两方面看待拜占庭。那种信仰就是我们所谓的正教，这两方面都不受尊重。按这样的看法，谁要说拜占庭人名副其实是罗马人，而且不仅在帝号延续这种抽象意义上是罗马人，在族群意义上也是罗马人，就会被视为荒唐。拜占庭人说希腊语，并不统治罗马，也不是罗马天主教徒，由此就被认为在语言（乃至族群性）、地理和宗教上都与罗马无关。对很多人来说，这种看法成了“心灵的壁纸”，
成了“最根深蒂固、往往根本未受审视的直觉”。
可是，最显而易见、最自然的立场有时恰恰最受意识形态左右。原本讲道理的历史学家，为了否认拜占庭人的罗马性，硬要把论证拗得难以自圆其说，就因为他们更相信“直觉”的前提，胜过史料中明白的证据。

en: This perspective was distinctive to the west but was adopted by many medieval Slavs too, who had closer ties to the medieval west than many scholars realize.
The Byzantines themselves, by contrast, consistently claimed that they were Romans. Had their
survived to modern times and developed its own scholarly traditions, there would inevitably have been a reckoning between it and these western ideologies. I suspect that these hypothetical modern
would have gained the upper hand and forced some recognition of their claim. The Arabs, who did not share in Latin biases, also regarded the Byzantines as

(Romans). In fact, in order to claim the ancient Greek intellectual tradition for themselves and deny it to the Greek-speakers of their own time, some Arab intellectuals were keen to deny precisely that the Byzantines were Greeks, because they were their rivals for the ownership of that tradition.

This was a different kind of denialism. Arab histories presented an alternative Byzantium, more accurate in some ways than the Latin version and more distorted in others, but the key point here is that they had no doubts that it was Roman. Yet for better or for worse, Byzantine Studies is a western artifact, not an Arab one, and was designed to buttress and promote western ideological claims.
zh: 这种看法原是西方所特有的，但许多中世纪斯拉夫人也接受了它，他们和中世纪西方的联系比不少学者所认识到的更紧密。
拜占庭人自己则始终坚称他们是罗马人。倘若他们的
（genos）延续到现代，并发展出自己的学术传统，终究会与西方的这些意识形态正面交锋。我猜，在这个假设里，现代的
（Romaioi）会占上风，迫使人们在一定程度上承认他们的自我认定。阿拉伯人不抱拉丁人的偏见，也把拜占庭人看作“
”（Rum，即罗马人）。事实上，有些阿拉伯知识分子为了把古希腊思想传统据为己有，不承认同时代讲希腊语的人有继承权，尤其要否认拜占庭人是希腊人，因为他们正是争夺这份传统的对手。
这是另一种否认论。阿拉伯史书呈现的拜占庭，有些地方比拉丁版本更准确，有些地方则更失实。关键在于，阿拉伯史家从不怀疑它是罗马的。无论好坏，拜占庭研究是西方所造，而非阿拉伯世界所造，其设计是为了巩固和推动西方的意识形态主张。

en: Until the later nineteenth century, the standard names for Byzantium in western historiography were “empire of Constantinople” and “empire of the Greeks.” The term
while coined in the sixteenth century and put to occasional use after that,

displaced the medieval terms only after around 1850 and through a process that is poorly understood; in fact, hardly anyone knows how crucial the nineteenth century was in this story because of the prevailing error that “Byzantium” became dominant in the sixteenth.

I suspect that among the reasons for this switch to Byzantium was the creation of a modern Greek state in the 1820s. By midcentury, the Greeks were agitating to reclaim Constantinople and re-create the “Greek empire” that was their birthright. Because such a state would have come at the expense of the Ottoman empire, the weakest link in the fragile post-Napoleonic imperial order, western powers were opposed to this idea, and some even perceived it as a Russian plot. The Crimean War, which was fought against Russia by France and Britain, two states that played a foundational role in the development of western scholarship about Byzantium, led to an intensification of Russophobia in the west and the fear that the tsar was using his Orthodox clients in the Balkans to create a Russian-dominated Greek Orthodox empire centered on Constantinople.
The historiographical term

could be seen as legitimating these aspirations and fueling the Greeks’ Grand Vision of imperial instauration. “Byzantium,” by contrast, was more neutral and less inflammatory and gradually replaced the ethnic name for the empire after the Crimean War.
zh: 直到十九世纪后期，西方史学对拜占庭的惯用名称还是“君士坦丁堡帝国”和“希腊人的帝国”。“
”一词虽创于十六世纪，此后也偶尔有人用，
但直到大约1850年以后才取代中世纪的称呼，其中的过程还不甚明了。事实上，盛行的误解是“拜占庭”在十六世纪就占了主导地位，因此几乎无人知道十九世纪在这段历史中有多关键。

我猜，改用“拜占庭”的一个原因是现代希腊国家于十九世纪二十年代建立。到世纪中叶，希腊人积极主张夺回君士坦丁堡，重建他们认为本来就属于自己的“希腊帝国”。建立这样一个国家会以奥斯曼帝国的损失为代价，而后者正是拿破仑战争后脆弱的帝国秩序中最薄弱的一环。西方列强因此反对这个主张，有人甚至认为这是俄国的阴谋。法国和英国在克里米亚战争中与俄国交战，这两个国家也在西方拜占庭学术形成之初起过奠基作用。战争加深了西方对俄国的恐惧，人们担心沙皇正利用他在巴尔干的正教附庸，建立一个以君士坦丁堡为中心、由俄国主导的希腊正教帝国。
史学术语“
”可能被视为给这些诉求以正当性，甚至助长希腊人重建帝国的“伟大理想”。“拜占庭”相对中立，较少引起纷争，便在克里米亚战争之后逐步取代了这个帝国的族群名称。

en: Thus, whereas western historiography had, until ca. 1800, accepted the continuity of “Greek” ethnic history from antiquity to the present, including Byzantium within this continuum,

when Byzantine Studies developed as a scholarly discipline in the later nineteenth and twentieth centuries this notion was no longer part of its core paradigm. The Greek ethnic element was played down, which is why our histories still refer to ethnically neutral “Byzantines,” a fictitious generic category that avoids the complications of both the Roman and the Greek labels. The emphasis was instead placed on imperial ideology and on Orthodoxy. Whereas surveys of Byzantium written in the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries saw it as the medieval state of the Greeks, in the twentieth century the emphasis shifted to it being an “Orthodox” empire and society. The baton of Hellenic continuity was passed, in the mid- to later nineteenth century, to nationalist historians of the new Greek state. Still, the “Greek” option abides as a fallback position within the western scholarly tradition,
though ultimately it can be only a loose way of talking as it is not backed by any theory of ethnicity or proof. “Greeks” can be only a temporary placeholder,
for Those Who Must Not Be Named.
zh: 因此，西方史学直到约1800年仍承认“希腊人”的族群史自古及今相承，并把拜占庭放进这条连续脉络。

但到了十九世纪后期和二十世纪，拜占庭研究发展为一门学科时，这种看法已不在其核心范式之内。希腊族群要素被淡化，我们的历史书至今仍用不标明族群的“拜占庭人”。这个虚构的统称避开了“罗马人”和“希腊人”这两个称谓牵涉的麻烦。学界转而强调帝国意识形态和正教。十八世纪和十九世纪初的拜占庭通史将其视为希腊人的中世纪国家，二十世纪却着重说那是一个“正教的”帝国和社会。到十九世纪中后期，维护希腊人历史连续性的任务转由新希腊国家的民族主义史家承担。不过，“希腊人”作为备用选项依然留在西方学术传统中。
由于没有族群理论或证据支撑，归根结底它只能是一种宽泛的说法。“希腊人”是退而求其次（
）的权宜称呼，用来指那些不可直呼其名的人。

en: In some quarters, the Greekness of Byzantium was not only softpedaled or quietly dropped, it was aggressively rejected. A virulent Slavophobic agenda led the German historian Jakob Philipp Fallmerayer (1790–1861) to deny that any racial continuity existed between the ancient and the modern Greeks. In his view, Byzantium had been taken over by Slavs and Albanians who half-learned how to speak Greek and whose descendants were masquerading as modern Hellenes.

As is well known, this attack prompted modern Greek historians to rehabilitate and appropriate Byzantium as a medieval Hellenic empire in order to buttress Greek racial continuity. Thus, as the west was moving away from the paradigm of the “Greek empire” and toward the ethnically vague notion of Byzantium, nationalist historiography in Greece ensconced the old ethnic model in its official view of the past. While there is skepticism about this model in Greece today, the empire’s official Hellenization in national discourse was possible only because western historiography had already stripped it of its Romanness. Some Greek national historians still go through the same motions of dismissing the testimony of the sources and ridiculing the idea that Greek-speaking Orthodox people can “really” be Romans. By stripping off that false label, they hope to expose the Greek underneath.
These moves were pioneered by western medieval writers and are still with us. For different reasons, therefore, both western and national Greek historiography have an interest to engage in denialism.
zh: 在某些圈子里，有人不止淡化或悄悄舍弃拜占庭的希腊性，还激烈地否定它。出于强烈的反斯拉夫立场，德国史家雅各布·菲利普·法尔默赖尔（1790–1861）否认古代与现代希腊人之间有任何种族连续性。在他看来，斯拉夫人和阿尔巴尼亚人已占据拜占庭，他们只学会了半生不熟的希腊语，他们的后裔却冒充今日的希腊人（Hellenes）。

众所周知，这一攻击促使现代希腊史家为拜占庭恢复名誉，把它收归为中世纪的希腊帝国，以维护希腊人的种族连续性。因此，西方正在弃用“希腊帝国”的范式，转向族群含义模糊的“拜占庭”，希腊的民族主义史学却把旧有的族群模式纳入官方历史观。今天希腊也有人质疑这一模式，不过，官方的民族叙事之所以能把帝国希腊化，恰恰是因为西方史学早已剥去了它的罗马性。部分撰写希腊民族史的史家仍在采取同样的做法，摒弃史料证词，嘲笑说希腊语、信正教的人怎么可能“真的”是罗马人。他们希望，只要剥去那个虚假的称号，就能露出底下的希腊人。
中世纪西方作者首开先河，这套做法一直延续到今天。因此，西方史学和希腊民族史学虽各有理由，却都有奉行否认论的利益。

en: In sum, the western names for Byzantium during the past thousand years were the products of politics, ideology, and powerful interests, ranging from the papacy and German emperors to the Great Powers of modernity. Their goal was not to promote understanding but to prevent Byzantium from getting in the way of ideological projects. We have still not escaped from this framework.
zh: 总之，过去一千年里西方给拜占庭起的名字，都是政治、意识形态和强大利益的产物，从教皇、德意志皇帝直到现代列强。它们的目标不是促进理解，而是防止拜占庭妨碍意识形态工程。我们至今仍未逃出这一框架。

en: The Quandaries of Denialism
zh: 否认论的困境

en: Two opposing forces tug at us when we consider the Romanness of Byzantium, and a synthesis of the two appears to be logically impossible. Scholars who step between them are inevitably wrenched in contradictory directions and end up in contorted positions. The first and historically dominant of these two forces is the denial of the Byzantines’ Romanness. This position finds it absurd—literally and intuitively nonsensical—to believe that Byzantium and the Byzantines were Roman in a meaningful sense. The second position is reflected in the Byzantine sources, according to which not only the empire in general but also the majority of its population were ethnically Romans. In the sources, and for anyone who follows them, this position is uncontroversial and intuitive. The Byzantines
Romans. They did not merely “call themselves” by that name in an artificial way or to deceive someone who was looking in.
zh: 当我们思考拜占庭的罗马性时，两股相反的力量拉扯着我们，而两者的综合在逻辑上似乎不可能。踏入两者之间的学者不可避免地被扯向矛盾的方向，最终落得扭曲的姿态。两股力量中第一股、也是历史上占主导的，是否认拜占庭人的罗马性。这一立场觉得，相信拜占庭和拜占庭人在任何有意义的意义上是罗马的，是荒谬的——字面地和直觉地都讲不通。第二股立场反映在拜占庭史料中：按照史料，帝国本身固然是罗马的，其中多数居民也在族群意义上属于罗马人。在史料中，对任何跟随史料的人来说，这一立场毫无争议、合乎直觉。拜占庭人
罗马人。他们并非只是假托这一称谓，或用来自称以欺骗旁观者。

en: There is no viable middle ground between these two positions, and efforts to mediate between them produce only weirder variations. That is why the state of the field regarding this question is chaotic and why positions are taken on seemingly arbitrary grounds. I will give one illustration. Before World War II, George Ostrogorsky, a Russian historian active in Serbia, wrote a history of Byzantium in German that became a standard work for decades afterward. In it, he correctly defined the Byzantine way of life as the product of three main elements: Roman, Greek, and Christian, which interacted in different ways and occupied different parts of the culture.

This banal definition long formed the basis for college courses and general discussions of Byzantium. It is repeated, for example, by a contributor to a small introductory volume written for nonexperts to celebrate the Dumbarton Oaks Research Center. A second contributor to that same volume, however, who advocates a Greek reading of Byzantium, states that the empire had only “a double nature”: Greek and Christian.

This demotion to two elements is not exclusive to Greek historians. In a general introduction to the Byzantines, Averil Cameron, a professor of Byzantine history in the United Kingdom, stated that their culture was based on two elements: Greek and Judeo-Christian. Yet later in the book she states that the Byzantines continued to refer to themselves as Romans. The strange implication is that the collective name by which they referred to themselves, along with its historical, political, and possibly ethnic connotations, did not count as one of the constituent elements of their culture.
zh: 这两种立场之间没有可行的中间地带，调和两者的努力只会产生更怪异的变种。这就是为什么本学科在这个问题上状态混乱，为什么立场的取舍看似任意。我举一个例子。二战前，活跃于塞尔维亚的俄国史学家乔治·奥斯特洛戈尔斯基用德文写了一部拜占庭史，此后数十年成为标准著作。他在书中正确地把拜占庭生活方式定义为三种主要要素的产物：罗马的、希腊的、基督教的，三者以不同的方式相互作用，各自涉及文化的不同方面。
这个平淡的定义长期构成大学课程和拜占庭一般讨论的基础。例如，一部为纪念敦巴顿橡树园研究中心、面向普通读者编写的入门小册子的一位撰稿人就重复了它。然而同一本书的另一位撰稿人把拜占庭解释为希腊文明，声称帝国只有“双重性质”：希腊的与基督教的。
这种降为两要素的做法并非希腊史学家独有。英国拜占庭史教授阿夫里尔·卡梅伦在一部拜占庭通论中说，他们的文化基于两种要素：希腊的与犹太—基督教的。可是她在书的后文又说，拜占庭人继续自称罗马人。奇怪的言下之意是：他们用以自称的集体名称，连同其历史的、政治的、可能还有族群的含义，竟不算他们文化的构成要素之一。

en: When Ostrogorsky referred to Byzantium’s Roman aspect, he meant “the Roman imperial framework,” a more limited conception of its valence than will be advocated in this book. According to his model, the Byzantines, whatever their ethnicity, actively engaged with or passively lived within a formally Roman structure of government. But even this limited notion is subject to apparently random revisions. For example, Cameron, without offering any elaboration, says that “the Byzantine administration was Greek in character.”

This is perplexing, as there was nothing like the Byzantine administration in previous Greek history and its practices derived entirely from Roman imperial administration. Besides, how is an administration “Greek in character”? This corresponds to no analytical category known to classicists or Hellenists.
zh: 奥斯特洛戈尔斯基提到拜占庭的罗马面向时，指的是“罗马帝国框架”，这比本书将阐述的罗马性意涵更为有限。按照他的模型，拜占庭人无论族群为何，都主动参与或被动生活在一个形式上罗马的政府结构之中。但即便这个有限的观念也遭到看似随意的修改。例如，卡梅伦没有任何展开就说，“拜占庭行政在性质上是希腊的”。
这令人困惑，因为此前的希腊历史上没有任何类似拜占庭行政的东西，其实践完全源自罗马帝国行政。再说，一个行政机构如何“在性质上是希腊的”？这不对应古典学家或希腊研究者熟悉的任何分析范畴。

en: The reason behind these variations and seeming arbitrariness is that the field has not yet had a scholarly discussion of the problem of the Romanness of Byzantium, a discussion in which models are based on the primary evidence, terms are defined, evidence is analyzed as to the scope of its relevance, and rival views are juxtaposed and evaluated. There is no body of critical scholarship to act as a center of gravity for a sustained systematic discussion. In its absence, unexamined intuitions fill the gap. This section will offer a critical survey of the denialist trend in Byzantine scholarship, which, for all the havoc it has caused, is not without an amusing side. I will map the terrain of opinion, highlighting its failures and quandaries by using mostly recent publications in English, although comparable moves are made in all relevant languages. I make no bones about belonging to the Romanist camp, which I discuss at the end. Even proponents of an authentically Roman Byzantium have not defined their position precisely or consistently, leaving it too in an inchoate state.
zh: 各种说法之所以出入不一，理由又似乎很随意，是因为本学科尚未就拜占庭的罗马性展开学术讨论，做到以一手史料为依据建立模型、界定术语、分析证据可以支持多大范围的判断，并将不同观点放在一起评估。不存在一个批判性学术整体，可以作为持续系统讨论的重心。在它缺席之处，未经审视的直觉填补了空白。本节将对拜占庭学术中的否认论倾向作一番批判性考察；尽管它造成了种种混乱，却也不乏有趣的一面。我会梳理各种观点，主要以近年英语著作为例，指出它们的缺陷和困境，不过以其他相关语言写成的研究也有类似做法。我毫不讳言自己属于主张拜占庭确实是罗马的一派，结尾将谈到这一立场。即便是真正罗马的拜占庭的主张者，也没有精确或一贯地界定自己的立场，使它同样处于未成形的状态。

en: The denialist position is basically only a continuation and rationalization of western medieval views of Byzantium. It is, moreover, utterly unselfconscious and unreflective of this fact. It has never critically examined the origins of its basic assumptions and does not know its own history, of which I offered an extremely condensed summary in the previous section. In treating its biases as natural and intuitive truths, the denialist position is strictly ideological. But these biases are contingent upon specific choices. Had German emperors and medieval popes not developed imperial ideologies of their own that lay exclusive claim to the Roman tradition, setting into motion an avalanche of polemic against the eastern empire, there would be no “Byzantium” in our history books today, no bizarre claims that the Byzantines lied or deluded themselves into thinking that they were Romans. This tradition of denial is unusual in a number of ways, and I will mention one here. A problem in many scholarly fields is that experts identify too closely with their subjects and reproduce their views uncritically, for example when Greek historians highlight the glories of ancient Hellenism or when Roman historians “side” with ancient Roman imperialism. In the case of Byzantine Studies, it is the reverse: through an academic equivalent of Stockholm syndrome, the field has adopted the perspective of those who denied Byzantine claims, derided the empire, destroyed it, and then denigrated it for centuries.
zh: 否认论立场基本上只是西方中世纪拜占庭观的延续与合理化。而且，它对这一事实完全不自知、不反思。它从未批判地考察自己基本假设的起源，也不了解自己的历史——上一节我已给出一个极度压缩的概述。否认论把偏见当作合乎直觉、不言而喻的真理，是一种彻头彻尾的意识形态立场。但这些偏见取决于特定的选择。假如德意志皇帝和中世纪教皇没有发展出自己的帝国意识形态、对罗马传统提出排他性主张，从而引发铺天盖地的反东部帝国论战，今天我们的历史书里就不会有“拜占庭”，也不会有拜占庭人撒谎或自我迷惑以为自己是罗马人的离奇说法。这一否认传统在若干方面很不寻常，这里只提一点。许多学术领域的问题是专家与自己的研究对象认同过深，不加批判地复制其观点，例如希腊史学家突出古代希腊主义的荣光，或研究罗马的历史学家“站在”古罗马帝国主义一边。拜占庭研究的情况恰恰相反：通过一种学术版的斯德哥尔摩综合征，本学科采纳了那些否认拜占庭主张、嘲弄帝国、摧毁帝国、然后又诋毁它数百年的人的视角。

en: One formulation of medieval denialism, that by the German emperor Louis II in 871, shows both how similar it is to its modern counterparts and how problematic western medieval assumptions could be to begin with. The specific diplomatic context was one of those recurring altercations between the western and eastern emperors (in this case the great-grandson of Charlemagne, Louis II, and Basileios I, the founder of the Macedonian dynasty) over their titles and rights to the Roman mantle. Louis could go only so far as to call Basileios the “emperor of New Rome,” while calling himself “emperor of the Romans” (this concession—that Constantinople was also Rome in its own way—would become increasingly hard to sustain in the west in later centuries). In brief, Louis argues that he has the right to be called emperor of the Romans and Basileios does not. Along the way, he makes some arguments that may strike us as modern, by which I mean only that they appear in modern scholarship. Modern scholars do not take them from Louis’ letter, which few read, but from a common store of misleading ideas.
zh: 中世纪否认论的一个表述——871年德意志皇帝路易二世的表述——既显示它与现代对应物多么相似，也显示西方中世纪的假设从一开始就多么成问题。具体的外交背景，是东西方皇帝之间反复发生的争执之一（这次是查理曼的曾孙路易二世与马其顿王朝的创立者瓦西里一世），围绕他们的头衔和对罗马衣钵的权利。路易至多肯称瓦西里为“新罗马的皇帝”，同时自称“罗马人的皇帝”（这一让步——君士坦丁堡也以自己的方式是罗马——在后来几个世纪的西方将越来越难维持）。简言之，路易论证自己有权被称为罗马人的皇帝，而瓦西里没有。其间他提出的一些论证可能让我们觉得现代——我的意思只是它们出现在现代学术中。现代学者不是从路易的信里取得这些论证的（很少有人读那封信），而是继承了同一批流传下来的错误观念。

en: Our concern is not with the arguments that Louis advances in support of his own claim to the title of Roman emperor, but with the arguments that he makes toward the middle of his letter against Basileios’ claim to it. “The Greeks,” he states,
zh: 我们关心的不是路易为支持自己对罗马皇帝头衔的主张而提出的论证，而是他在信的中段针对瓦西里的同一主张提出的论证。他说，“希腊人”——

en: have ceased to be emperors of the Romans on account of their bad opinions when it comes to religious faith. Also, not only have they abandoned the city and the seat of empire [Rome], they have also abandoned the Roman people [i.e., of Rome] and the language itself [Latin], having migrated in all ways to a different city, seat, people, and language [Greek].
zh: 因为他们在信仰上的看法有误，已经不再是罗马人的皇帝。他们不但抛弃了那座城和帝国的中心［罗马］，也抛弃了罗马人民［即罗马城的人民］和语言本身［拉丁语］。在各个方面，他们都转向了另一座城、另一个中心、另一群人民和另一种语言［希腊语］。

en: Louis and other western writers offered additional arguments against the Greeks’ claim to the imperial Roman title, but these modern scholars would be reluctant to reproduce. For example, Louis maintains that he has a better claim to the title because it was bestowed on him by the pope, whereas in the east the so-called emperors were sometimes acclaimed by the senate, the people, and the armies.
In making this argument, Louis displayed how out of touch he was with ancient Roman tradition. In this particular aspect, eastern practice adhered to authentic Roman notions of acclamation,
whereas western practice did not; and only a staunch Catholic theorist would support a theory of imperial legitimacy through papal coronation. To give another example, the western
claimed that the imperial title was available to be assumed by Charlemagne because the eastern ruler at the time was a woman, Eirene, who clearly did not count, making the throne effectively vacant.
None of this is relevant anymore, nor is Louis’ claim that the “Greeks” had lost the right to the Roman title because of their bad religious opinions.
zh: 路易和其他西方作家还提出一些理由来反驳“希腊人”拥有罗马帝号的主张，不过现代学者大概不愿重述这些理由。例如，路易坚持自己更有资格拥有这个头衔，因为它是教皇授予的，而在东方，所谓皇帝有时是由元老院、人民和军队欢呼拥立的。
提出这一论证时，路易显示了他与古罗马传统多么脱节。恰恰在这个方面，东方的实践遵循了真正的罗马欢呼拥立观念，
而西方的实践没有；只有坚定的天主教理论家才会支持认为教皇加冕可以授予皇权合法性的理论。再举一例：西方的《洛尔施编年史》声称，查理曼可以取得皇帝头衔，因为当时的东方统治者是个女人伊琳娜，她显然不算数，皇位实际上空缺。
这一切如今都不再相关，路易关于“希腊人”因宗教意见错误而丧失罗马头衔权利的说法也不再相关。

en: The part of Louis’ letter that codified the bedrock of western denialism for centuries is its claims about ethnicity, speech, and geography. Louis assumes that Basileios’ subjects are “Greeks” and calls them that throughout the letter. While he concedes that an emperor of the Romans could be appointed from among the Greeks, Spaniards, or Franks, he promotes the city of Rome as the deciding criterion, in part because it theoretically fell within his realm and also because his letter was possibly ghost-written by Anastasius the Librarian, a native of Rome who had an ax to grind against Byzantium.
Basileios could not be emperor of the Romans because his people were not Romans either by ethnicity or language and also because Basileios did not hold the city of Rome.
zh: 路易信中为西方否认论奠定数百年基石的部分，是其关于族群、语言和地理的主张。路易预设瓦西里的臣民是“希腊人”，并在整封信中这样称呼他们。他虽承认罗马人的皇帝可以从希腊人、西班牙人或法兰克人中任命，却把罗马城提升为决定性标准，部分因为该城理论上在他的版图之内，也因为他的信可能由图书馆员阿纳斯塔修斯代笔——此人是罗马本地人，对拜占庭怀有私怨。
瓦西里不能做罗马人的皇帝，因为他的人民在族群上并非罗马人，说的也并非罗马语，也因为瓦西里不占有罗马城。

en: Similar views were expressed by Liudprand of Cremona, who visited the court of Nikephoros II Phokas as an emissary of the German emperor in 968 and wrote a satirical and hostile account of his experience. When Nikephoros was angry at the pope for addressing him as emperor of the Greeks, Liudprand disingenuously responded that the pope had actually wanted to flatter him: yes, Constantinople had been founded by Romans, but since you have now changed the language, customs, and dress, the pope feared that he might offend by calling you Romans.

Liudprand knew perfectly that the Byzantines called themselves Romans, and only pretended that he was surprised to hear it. What is important, however, is that he too frames the issue as one of ethnicity, pointing to language, customs, and dress. In the eyes of a western observer, these indicia proved that the Byzantines were Greeks.
zh: 克雷莫纳的利乌特普兰德表达过类似观点。他968年作为德意志皇帝的使节访问尼基弗鲁斯二世·福卡斯的宫廷，并写下游记，语带讽刺、充满敌意。当尼基弗鲁斯因教皇称他为希腊人的皇帝而发怒时，利乌特普兰德不诚实地回应说，教皇其实是想奉承他：不错，君士坦丁堡是罗马人建立的，但既然你们如今改变了语言、习俗和服饰，教皇担心称你们为罗马人会冒犯你们。
利乌特普兰德完全知道拜占庭人自称罗马人，只是假装听到这话很惊讶。然而重要的是，他也把问题框定为族群问题，指向语言、习俗和服饰。在西方观察者眼中，这些迹象证明拜占庭人是希腊人。

en: Consider how little had changed by the time of Gibbon, eight hundred years later. For Gibbon, “the Franks and Latins . . . asserted, with some justice, their superior claim to the language and dominion of Rome. They insulted the aliens of the east who had renounced the dress and idiom of Romans; and their reasonable practice will justify the frequent appellation of Greeks” [i.e., by Gibbon himself in his narrative].
zh: 到八百年后的吉本那里，情形几乎没变。吉本说：“法兰克人和拉丁人……声称对罗马的语言和统治权享有优先的权利，这不无道理。他们侮辱东方那些抛弃了罗马人服饰与语言的外人。他们这样做合乎情理，足以说明为何常用‘希腊人’来称呼对方”［即吉本在自己的叙述里用的称呼］。

en: One goal of this book will be to argue that these assumptions, especially when converted into quasi-scholarly arguments by modern historians, reflect a mistaken view of Roman identity; are not grounded in the Roman tradition that Byzantium inherited from antiquity; and directly contradict fundamental axioms of modern research in the humanities and social sciences, especially regarding ethnic identities. Before delving into the heart of the case, I want to illustrate the persistence of these views across wide swaths of the field and the invidious ways in which they work. Anyone who has read much Byzantine scholarship will have encountered them many times, but it is still illuminating to see medieval biases echoed by scholars, who profess to be baffled at the Byzantines for continuing to “call themselves Romans” when we supposedly know that they “really” were not. For example, the holder of a named chair in Byzantine Studies wrote that “the inhabitants of the successor empire in Constantinople paradoxically never ceased to refer to themselves as Romans—paradoxically because the language of administration and literature was . . . Greek.”

Others echo the claim that the empire was cut off from the alleged “source of its ideology,” meaning the Roman west, or “cut off from the cradle of its Roman ideology, the city of Rome.” Yet even after that its inhabitants still “stubbornly” called themselves Romans.
zh: 本书的目标之一，是论证这些假设——尤其当它们被现代史学家转化为半学术论证时——反映了对罗马认同的错误看法；并不植根于拜占庭从古代继承的罗马传统；并且直接违背现代人文与社会科学研究的基本公理，尤其是关于族群认同的公理。在深入讨论本书的核心论证之前，我想先展示这些观点在本学科广大范围内的持续存在，以及它们运作的阴险方式。任何读过大量拜占庭学术著作的人都已多次遇到它们，但看到中世纪偏见被学者们回声般重复，仍很有启发：这些学者说，他们不明白拜占庭人为什么继续“自称罗马人”，仿佛我们早已知道他们“其实”并非罗马人。例如，一位拜占庭研究冠名讲席教授写道：“令人费解的是，君士坦丁堡这个继承帝国的居民从未停止自称罗马人。说这令人费解，是因为行政与文学所用的语言是……希腊语。”
另一些人重复说，帝国与其所谓“意识形态之源”——即罗马西方——隔绝了，或“与其罗马意识形态的摇篮罗马城隔绝了”。然而即便如此，其居民仍“顽固地”自称罗马人。

en: The criterion of “Italy” is interesting because it exposes both the origins of modern denialism and the hypocrisy at its heart. Rome and Italy had ceased to be the deciding or even a relevant criterion of Romanness already in the second century ad, as Romans at the time had already realized: a Roman general of Antiochene origin even said that “Rome was wherever the emperor was.”
In the third century, Romans filled the entire empire, emperors stopped living in Rome or even visiting it, and they began to call their provincial capitals “Rome.” Rome was now a world, not a city.

No contemporary source for the fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, or eighth century suggests that to be Roman you had to live in Rome, be from Rome, or control Rome, and no modern scholar of those centuries thinks so either. In a period when the emperors came from the provinces and spent their entire reigns there, St. Jerome declared that, when it came to (Roman) authority, “the world outweighs the city.”

But when popes and German emperors in the ninth century begin to assert the centrality of Rome to Romanness, suddenly and conveniently modern scholars also discover that lost criterion and use it to discredit Byzantine claims to Romanness. Needless to say, the eastern Romans, who were the product of the globalization of Romanness between the second and the fourth centuries, were unaware of this criterion.
zh: “意大利”这一标准很有意思，因为它既暴露了现代否认论的起源，也暴露了其核心的虚伪。罗马和意大利早在公元二世纪就已不再是罗马性的决定性标准、甚至不再是相关标准，当时的罗马人已经意识到这一点：一位安条克出身的罗马将军甚至说，“皇帝在哪里，罗马就在哪里”。
三世纪时，罗马人遍布整个帝国，皇帝们不再住在罗马、甚至不再到访罗马，并开始把自己的行省首府称为“罗马”。罗马至此已是一个世界，而非一座城市。
四、五、六、七、八世纪的任何同时代史料都不曾暗示：要做罗马人，你必须住在罗马、来自罗马或控制罗马；研究这些世纪的现代学者也没有人这样认为。在皇帝来自行省、整个在位期间都待在行省的时代，圣耶柔米宣称，就（罗马）权威而言，“世界重于城市”。
但当九世纪的教皇和德意志皇帝开始主张罗马对罗马性的核心地位时，现代学者也恰好突然发掘出了这个失落的标准，并用它来贬损拜占庭对罗马性的主张。不用说，随着罗马性在二至四世纪扩展到整个帝国而形成的东方罗马人，并不知道这个标准。

en: In order to deny Byzantine Romanness, some modern historians defend the invented term
as appropriate not only for the sake of convention or as only a period of Roman history, but on substantive grounds, because—I have italicized some crucial words—
zh: 为了否认拜占庭的罗马性，一些现代史学家为发明的术语“拜占庭帝国”辩护，说它恰当不只是出于约定俗成、或只作为罗马史的一个分期，而是有实质理由的，因为——我把一些关键词加了斜体——

en: it underlines that both empire and people were distinct from their Roman forerunners—

children: it does not matter that the Byzantines almost always called it the Roman Empire and themselves Romans.

en: The essence of this distinction between Roman and Byzantine is to be found in the capital city of Byzantium, where a new culture and political system were forged out of old materials. . . . Abandoning Rome and the West to the barbarians meant that
—what it meant to be a Roman—was being drained of meaning.
zh: 它强调帝国和人民都不同于其罗马前身——

children: 拜占庭人几乎总是称它为罗马帝国、称自己为罗马人，但这无关紧要

zh: 。罗马与拜占庭何以判然有别，要到拜占庭的都城去寻找，那里用旧材料锻造出一种新文化和新政治制度……任罗马和西方落入蛮族之手，就意味着
（Romanitas），即身为罗马人所具有的意义，正在消失。

en: The resemblance between ancient Rome and Byzantium is described by the same historian as “superficial and schematic,” a mere “illusion of the continuing unity of the Roman world around Constantinople.”

This is then washed down with disparaging comments, another legacy of the Enlightenment: “Byzantium turned out to be the weakest of the medieval civilizations, with the least to offer in terms of originality and development.”
We should turn to Venice if want to find true splendor.
zh: 古代罗马与拜占庭的相似性被同一位史学家描述为“表面而图式化的”，不过是“罗马世界围绕君士坦丁堡持续统一的幻觉”。
接着又佐以贬损性评论——启蒙运动的另一份遗产：“拜占庭结果成了中世纪诸文明中最弱的一个，在原创性与发展方面贡献最少。”
若要寻找真正的辉煌，我们应该转向威尼斯。

en: Denialism has, then, developed its own terms of art, such as “Byzantium,” along with specialized methods of evasion. The most common method in introducing the Byzantines is to say that they “called themselves” or “referred to themselves” as Romans, but for the modern historian to not then call them that herself. This is done, for example on the first page of the recent

A corollary of this practice is to put the name “Romans” in quotation marks. This is a truly weird habit, if we think for a moment what it would look like if applied to any other historical people who had a strongly held, widely attested, and quite serviceable name. It is also out of sync with modern efforts to restore indigenous names to groups that have been marginalized in western perceptions of history (e.g., Inuit for Eskimo). In the case of Byzantium, this odd practice of circumlocution and quotation marks plants invidious doubts about whether the Byzantines “really were” who they thought and said they were.
zh: 于是，否认论发展出自己的术语，如“拜占庭”，以及专门的回避方法。介绍拜占庭人时最常见的方法，是说他们“自称”或“称自己为”罗马人，但现代史学家自己随后却不这样称呼他们。例如，新近的《牛津拜占庭研究手册》第一页就是这样做的。

与此相伴的，是给“罗马人”这个名称加上引号。如果把这种做法用在任何另一个历史民族身上，想想对方一向坚持自称的名称在史料中广为可见、称呼起来也毫无困难，就会看出这习惯有多怪异。它也与现代为那些在西方历史认知中被边缘化的群体恢复本名的努力不合拍（例如用因纽特（Inuit）取代爱斯基摩（Eskimo））。就拜占庭而言，这种迂回说法加引号的古怪做法，埋下了阴险的怀疑：拜占庭人是否“真的是”他们自认为、自称的那个样子。

en: Denialism is often coupled with moral censure. A professor of Byzantine history writes that the Byzantines “pulled off one of the greatest deceptions in history, presenting their society in terms of absolute continuity with the past: to very end they insisted on describing themselves as ‘Romans’ as if nothing had changed since ancient times.”

For this historian, the fact of “change” makes the Byzantines’ claim to be Romans an act of deception. He does not, however, also present us with a methodology by which we can tell how much and what kind of change can support such a conclusion. Rome had “changed” also between Scipio and Cicero, Cicero and Hadrian, and Hadrian and Constantine. Even historians of ancient Rome these days are not sure how much continuity lies beneath the massive changes that the city experienced. As Harriet Flower put it, “How can the archaic community of the Romans be said to be the same republic as the one that conquered Carthage or the one described by Cicero?”

Either all should count as Roman, or we must reduce history to a series of unconnected microslices defined by ever narrower frames of reference. In coping with this problem, William Harris, a historian of ancient Rome, writes that, “Almost everything changes [in Roman history], not only the sources and the material culture, but the principal language and the dominant religion. But that is a challenge, not an excuse.”
Byzantium is part of that challenge, as Harris recognizes.
zh: 否认论常与道德谴责搭配。一位拜占庭史教授写道，拜占庭人“完成了历史上最大的欺骗之一，把自己的社会呈现为与过去绝对连续：直到最后他们仍坚持自称‘罗马人’，仿佛古代以来什么都没变”。

对这位史学家来说，“变化”的事实使拜占庭人自称罗马人成了欺骗行为。然而他并没有同时给我们一套方法论，让我们判断多大程度、何种类型的变化能支撑这样的结论。罗马在西庇阿与西塞罗之间、西塞罗与哈德良之间、哈德良与君士坦丁之间也“变化”过。如今连古罗马史学家都不确定，在这座城市经历的巨变之下有多少连续性。正如哈丽特·弗劳尔所说：“怎能说罗马人的古风共同体与征服迦太基的那个共和国、或西塞罗描述的那个共和国是同一个共和国？”
要么全都算罗马，要么我们必须把历史还原为一系列互不相连的微小切片，由越来越窄的参照框架定义。在处理这个问题时，古罗马史学家威廉·哈里斯写道：“几乎一切都在变［罗马史中］，不仅是史料和物质文化，还有主要语言和主导宗教。但那是挑战，不是借口。”
正如哈里斯所承认的，拜占庭是这一挑战的一部分。

en: A recent book-length study finds that what it meant to be Roman in antiquity varied by period, region, and context, and calls for the plural study of Roman
Emma Dench concludes that study with a warning that points directly, in my eyes, to Byzantium:
zh: 新近一部专书研究发现，在古代，身为罗马人的含义因时代、地区和语境而异，因此主张研究多样的罗马
（identities，复数）。艾玛·登奇以一段警告结束该书，在我眼中直接指向拜占庭：

en: Any notion of an “end” to my account of Roman identities is obviously problematic. We have, it is true, hinted at the emergence of strikingly different formulations of identity at the end of the period considered. . . . I would be very weary of positing a decisive break with the past, or a definitive shift towards “global” identities, or anything of the sort.
zh: 要说我对罗马认同的叙述可以有一个“终点”，显然会遇到问题。诚然，我们已指出，在所考察时期将尽之际，出现了截然不同的认同表述……但若要断言当时同过去彻底决裂，或明确转向“全球性”认同，或提出此类说法，我会非常谨慎。

en: In other words, modern scholars of ancient Rome—one standard by which we might evaluate the Romanness of Byzantium—are more open to change and variation within Roman tradition than are Byzantinists. The latter should have been leading the charge but, shamefully, have been in steady retreat. They may fear that claiming Byzantium as Roman will elicit resistance from historians of ancient Rome. Based on these recent studies, however, I expect that we will be pushing against an open door.
zh: 换言之，古罗马的现代研究者——我们可以用来评估拜占庭罗马性的一个标准——比拜占庭学家对罗马传统内部的变化与变异更开放。后者本应带头冲锋，却可耻地一直在稳步撤退。他们可能担心，把拜占庭认领为罗马会招致古罗马史学家的抵制。但基于这些新近研究，我想，我们所要说服的同行很可能早已认同这一点。

en: “Change” is one arbitrary criterion invented ad hoc to justify a preexisting prejudice. There are others. Some affirm that Byzantium was “too small” to be authentically Roman.

Again, there appears to be no methodology in the whole of Ancient Roman Studies that justifies this conclusion: How small can Rome get without ceasing to be Rome? No ancient historian has addressed this question. It is only an arbitrary criterion of what it means to be “authentically” Roman that is designed to exclude Byzantium. Here is another, even more bizarre, criterion: “The Greek East, despite its self-identification as ‘Roman,’ does not appear to have been concerned with oral sex at all.”
I admit that I cannot reconstruct the logic here. Other scholars have claimed that the sources of Byzantine law had lost the “spirit of Roman law,”
while an older study of Greek urbanism asserted that Constantinople ceased to be a Roman city because of the inherent evil of the Byzantine empire.
zh: “变化”是为证明既有偏见而特设发明的一个任意标准。还有别的。有人断言拜占庭“太小”，不配是真正的罗马。
同样，整个古罗马研究界似乎没有任何方法论能证明这一结论：罗马小到什么程度就不再是罗马？没有古代史学家处理过这个问题。它不过是为了排除拜占庭，随意规定何谓“真正的”罗马。这里还有另一个更离奇的标准：“希腊东方尽管自我认同为‘罗马’，却似乎根本不关心口交。”
我承认我无法重构这里的逻辑。另一些学者声称拜占庭法的渊源已丧失“罗马法的精神”，
而一部较早的希腊城市布局研究断言，君士坦丁堡因拜占庭帝国固有的邪恶而不再是罗马城市。

en: A claim such as that, made before World War II, may seem to have no place in our scholarship, and there is growing recognition among historians of the continuity between Rome and New Rome. Yet monographs and textbooks continue to rely on Enlightenment caricatures of Byzantium in order to periodize history in moral-political terms. Byzantium, for example, does not count as a real Rome because it was too despotic and oriental. It reached back to the empires of the ancient Near East in order to find models for its “distant ruler with a heavy hand brandishing a strong religious ideology . . . even more so than [it did to] the earlier Roman empire.” Another recent study calls Byzantium an autocratic and theocratic state that had moved from orthodoxy to fundamentalism and fused religion with politics in a way that would not be undone until the Enlightenment, whose roots lay in the medieval west. These are not cranky fringe publications but academic monographs published by mainstream presses.

Such perceptions are entrenched and widespread. The leading historian of the Hittites could write (in 2002) that the Hittites failed to produce anything like the “paranoid despots of imperial Rome . . . to say nothing of the succession of grotesque monsters who occupied the throne of Byzantium.”
I wrote to him and asked which monsters he had in mind, but I did not receive an answer. Moralizing views of history still inform scholarly periodizations.
zh: 这样一个二战前提出的主张，在我们的学术中似乎已无立足之地，而且史学家们越来越承认罗马与新罗马之间的连续性。然而专著和教科书仍依赖启蒙运动对拜占庭的漫画化，以便按道德—政治口径给历史分期。例如，拜占庭不算真正的罗马，因为它太专制、太东方。为了给它那位“高居远处、以重手统治、挥舞强势宗教意识形态的统治者”找范本，它回溯了古代近东各帝国，“……甚至比［回溯］早期罗马帝国更甚”。另一部新近研究称拜占庭是一个专制神权国家，从正统信仰走向原教旨主义，把宗教与政治融合在一起，直到启蒙运动才解开，而启蒙运动的根在中世纪西方。这些不是偏执的边缘出版物，而是主流出版社出版的学术专著。
这类看法根深蒂固、流传广泛。赫梯研究的头号史学家可以写道（2002年）：赫梯人没能产生任何类似“帝国罗马的偏执暴君……更不用说占据拜占庭皇位的那一连串怪诞怪物”的东西。
我写信问他指的是哪些怪物，但没有收到答复。道德化的历史观仍在支配学术分期。

en: The denialists’ criteria are so diverse—small, Greek, oriental, evil—that they are patently pretexts for a preexisting position. They are not drawing on some foundational study that rigorously established the case but are instead inventing ad hoc criteria to patrol the borders of a separation that they feel they must enforce. Their individual positions face substantial methodological problems. In no case do they offer supporting reasons why the criterion they choose is relevant or able, even if it were true, to prove that the Byzantines were not Romans. The most disarming evasion that I have come across recently, in a recent book on Byzantine collective identities no less, is that the name “Roman” could not be considered because there are simply too many attestations of it. After all, the author adds, it had to do only with imperial ideology and not identity.
This nicely illustrates how the modern view of Byzantine Romanness as an almost metaphysical concept inhibits research into its actual meaning.
zh: 否认论者的标准如此多样——小、希腊、东方、邪恶——显然是既有立场的借口。他们并不是援引某项已严谨证成这一结论的基础研究，而是临时造出标准，用来维持自己非守不可的区隔。他们各自的立场面临重大的方法论问题。没有一例给出支持性理由，说明所选标准为何相关、或即便属实为何能证明拜占庭人不是罗马人。我最近遇到的最让人卸防的回避——竟出自新近一部论拜占庭集体认同的书——是：“罗马”这个名称不能纳入考察，因为史料中有关它的记载实在太多。作者还补充说，毕竟它只与帝国意识形态有关，与认同无关。
这很好地说明，把拜占庭罗马性视为近乎形而上学概念的现代观点，如何阻碍了对它实际意义的研究。

en: Denialism results in baffling expressions, as historians try to occupy the nonexistent space between western prejudices and the unambiguous evidence of the Byzantine sources. We are told, for example, that despite their “shrunken circumstances,” the Byzantines “found it difficult to abandon their sense of being
‘Romans.’”
What offstage narrative is implied by this odd statement? It is as if some force were pushing them to abandon their sense of who they were, and they were

at the point of doing so, but in the end they could not quite bring themselves to do it. This sounds instead like a displaced metaphor for what is going on in modern scholarship: We would like to abandon the term

in dealing with the Byzantines, but we cannot quite do so, because it is written all over the sources. Consider also the emperor Herakleios, who, we are told, “did not consider his empire to be a Near Eastern state”—which is correct, because he lacked such a concept (so why is it mentioned?). Instead, “it was a Roman one, however vague that was in his mind.”

But we are not told why Herakleios would have had a vaguer notion of the Romanness of his empire than any previous emperor. In reality, it is we who have a vague understanding of the matter and project it onto them. Yet we pretend it is the other way around: that we know the real, inner, deeper truth about who the Byzantines really were, whereas they were trapped in outdated labels and self-deception.
zh: 否认论产生令人困惑的表述，因为史学家试图占据西方偏见与拜占庭史料明白证据之间那个不存在的空间。例如我们被告知，尽管“境况已大不如前”，拜占庭人“仍很难放弃自己是
（Rhomaioi）的认同”。
这句怪话暗示了怎样的幕后叙事？仿佛有某种力量在推着他们放弃对自身身份的认识，而他们
就要放弃了，但最终还是没能狠下心。这听起来更像是现代学术中正在发生之事的错位隐喻：我们想在处理拜占庭人时放弃“罗马”这个词，但又不太做得到，因为它写满了史料。再看看希拉克略皇帝，我们被告知，他“不认为自己的帝国是一个近东国家”——这没错，因为他没有这个概念（那为什么要提？）。相反，“它是一个罗马帝国，尽管这在他心中很模糊”。
但我们没有被告知，为什么希拉克略对自己帝国罗马性的观念会比任何前任皇帝更模糊。实际上，对这个问题理解不清的是我们，是我们把它投射到他们身上。然而我们假装事情相反：仿佛我们知道拜占庭人真正是谁的实在、内在、更深的真相，而他们被困在过时的标签和自我欺骗中。

en: As we have seen, denialism works its invidious ways through adverbs such as “stubbornly,” “paradoxically,” “vaguely,” and “technically.” “The Byzantines always termed themselves Romans, since their empire was the direct continuation of the ancient Roman empire, technically at least.”

Here a distinction is implied between who the Byzantines claimed they were, which is only a technicality, and some other putative essence of their identity that we know and they did not. But maybe they

know and were only pretending all along. In no less than the Presidential Address delivered at the American Philological Association meeting of 2004, it was asserted that Byzantium was only “outwardly Roman [and was] increasingly incoherent and unable to match its sense of self to its reality because it knew too clearly what it was and what it had been.”
Here the implication of deception is raised again, as the Byzantines seem to have known that they were no longer “really” Romans and that by 600 ad “all the
had gone out of it [their empire].”
The footnote to the published version of the address implies that in reality they were Greeks.
zh: 正如我们所见，否认论通过“顽固地”“令人费解地”“模糊地”“严格说来”之类的副词施展其阴险手段。“拜占庭人总是自称罗马人，因为他们的帝国是古罗马帝国的直接延续，至少严格说来如此。”
这里暗示了一种区分：拜占庭人自称是谁，只在狭义上算数；认同另有所谓本质，只有我们知晓，他们自己却不知情。但也许他们
知道，只是一直在装作不知道。在2004年美国语文学会年会上发表的会长演说中，竟有人断言，拜占庭只是“外表罗马，［并且］越来越不连贯，无法使自我感觉与现实相匹配，因为它太清楚自己是什么、曾经是什么”。
这里再次抬出欺骗的暗示，因为拜占庭人似乎知道自己不再“真的”是罗马人，知道到公元600年“一切
（romanitas）都已从它［他们的帝国］中流失”。
该演说发表版的脚注暗示，他们实际上是希腊人。

en: One modality of denialism for “containing” the Romanness of Byzantium is to restrict it to the rarefied space of imperial ideology and propaganda, as if it had nothing to do with the majority of the empire’s inhabitants. Byzantinists quickly reach for the emperor’s titles when they have to explain the appearance in the sources of the ethnonym “Romans.” The discussion can then be transposed to a theological level and linked to ecumenical visions, End-Time scenarios, God’s plan for the salvation of mankind, and the like.
In this way, the Roman name was a purely formal matter that operated “officially” (another one of those tricky adverbs).
It was a function of “the consciously antiquated language of the sources.”

This trope of a formal reality—that is, an unreal reality—is invoked when Byzantium exhibits traits that do not fit the model that scholars have constructed for it (including rationality, classicism, freedom, continuity, and the like). They are exorcised by being labeled as purely nominal, official, antiquarian, or “paradoxical.” This is a tool for sweeping away “stubborn” facts that do not fit the model. In our case, that fact is nothing less than who the Byzantines were.
zh: 否认论有一种限制拜占庭罗马性适用范围的办法，就是把它局限在帝国意识形态与宣传这个远离日常生活的领域，仿佛它与帝国的大多数居民无关。拜占庭学家需要解释史料为何出现“罗马人”这一族名时，常常立即搬出皇帝的头衔。接着，讨论就可以转到神学层面，围绕普世愿景、末世景象、上帝拯救世人的计划等展开。
这样一来，罗马称谓就成了纯属形式的东西，只在“官方”层面起作用（这又是个难以捉摸的副词）。
照这种说法，它的出现源于“史料刻意仿古的语言”。
拜占庭呈现出理性、古典主义、自由、连续性之类的特征，与学者为它建立的模型不合时，他们就会诉诸这种形式上的现实，亦即不真实的现实。只要把这些特征说成纯属名义、仅限官方、出于好古或“令人费解”，就可以把它们驱逐出去。这是用来扫去不合模型的“顽固”事实的手段。这里被扫去的事实恰恰关系到拜占庭人到底是谁。

en: In drawing a distinction between an “official” view of reality promulgated by the “antiquarian” texts of the court (on the one hand) and the identity of the majority of Byzantines (on the other), scholars are again implicitly following the lead of partisan medieval observers such as Louis II. Louis, we recall, intuitively saw the subjects of Basileios as “Greeks.” The only thing even

Roman that he saw in Byzantium were the titles and propaganda of the court, and even those he was concerned to deny. Likewise, a strain of modern scholarship views the Roman identity of Byzantium primarily in terms of “official” imperial theory, court titles, and diplomacy, a sphere that naturally excluded the majority of the population.
A variant of this position uses modern “critical theory” to argue that Roman identity in Byzantium was limited to the literary elite in Constantinople.

However, such conclusions can be drawn only in analytical frameworks from which most or all of the evidence has been excluded. As we will see, and as the field has always known, claims to Roman identity in Byzantium are abundant, extend in scope well beyond the court and elites, and consistently point in the opposite direction: the ethnicity or nationality of the majority of the population was Roman, as indicated already in the five snapshots presented at the head of this chapter.
zh: 在宫廷“好古”文本宣扬的“官方”看法与大多数拜占庭人的认同之间划出界线时，学者们其实已暗中沿用了路易二世等立场鲜明的中世纪论者的看法。我们记得，路易直觉地把瓦西里的臣民看作“希腊人”。在他眼中，拜占庭仅有宫廷的头衔和宣传还
算是罗马的，但他连这两样也急于否认。同样，一股现代学术主要按“官方”帝国理论、宫廷头衔和外交来看待拜占庭的罗马认同，而这个领域自然排除了人口的大多数。
这一立场的一个变种用现代“批判理论”论证，拜占庭的罗马认同仅限于君士坦丁堡的文学精英。
然而，这样的结论只能从排除了大部分或全部证据的分析框架中得出。我们将会看到——而且本学科一直知道——拜占庭有大量关于罗马认同的自我表述，远不限于宫廷与精英，并一致指向相反的结论：大多数居民属于罗马族群或民族，本章开头呈现的五幅剪影已经表明了这一点。

en: Who were the Byzantines, then?
zh: 那么，拜占庭人是谁？

en: One approach is to see them as a vast enigma. Consider a classic paper by Paul Magdalino, “Hellenism and Nationalism in Byzantium.” Magdalino presents a number of texts that strongly suggest that Byzantium was a nation-state and harbored forms of nationalism. He does not deny these impressions or even their reality, but he leaves the matter open when he finds that he cannot answer the question, “What ‘nation’ did it represent?” He does not consider the possibility that it might be the very nation—the Roman one—that his sources are constantly talking about. That group is simply not on his radar, so he concludes that “the question of ethnicity was left open,” which we have already seen was certainly not the case.
In this case, denialism has rendered the Romans invisible, as if they never existed.
zh: 一种进路是把他们看成一个巨大的谜。想想保罗·马格达利诺的经典论文《拜占庭的希腊主义与民族主义》。马格达利诺列举了若干文本，强烈暗示拜占庭是一个民族国家，并且存在某些形式的民族主义。他不否认这些印象、甚至不否认它们的真实性，但当他发现自己无法回答“它代表什么‘民族’？”这个问题时，就把事情悬置了。他没有考虑这样一种可能：它可能正是他的史料不断谈论的那个民族——罗马民族。他根本没有把这个群体纳入考察，于是他得出结论说“族群性问题被悬置了”，而我们已经看到事实绝非如此。
在这个案例中，否认论使罗马人隐形了，仿佛他们从未存在。

en: Another approach, which we have seen already, is to follow the western lead and call the Byzantines Greeks, or rather to characterize them as Greek in some loose way that does not call for a rigorous analysis of their ethnicity. With the exception of a tiny number of intellectuals in the later period, the Byzantines themselves did not think they were Greeks and resented the name, which was imposed on them by the Latins.

It is not a coincidence that the name Greeks is used for the Byzantines far more frequently by scholars who work on the later period of the empire. This is not because they follow the lead of those two or three Hellenizing Byzantine thinkers. Rather, the later period was when the Latins colonized the Byzantine world and left more sources about their “Greek” subjects, allies, and enemies, making it easier for historians to simply follow the western lead. Translations of Byzantine texts sometimes even render
as “Greek.”
zh: 另一种我们已经见过的进路，是跟随西方的指引称拜占庭人为希腊人，或者更确切地说，以某种松散的方式把他们描述为希腊的，而不要求对其族群性作严谨分析。除了后期极少数知识分子，拜占庭人自己并不认为自己是希腊人，而且憎恶这个名字——它是拉丁人强加给他们的。
研究帝国后期的学者远比其他人更频繁地用希腊人这个名字称呼拜占庭人，这并非巧合。原因并不在于他们追随那两三个倾向于希腊认同的拜占庭思想家。帝国后期，拉丁人殖民拜占庭世界，留下更多关于他们的“希腊”臣民、盟友和敌人的史料，历史学家也就更容易直接沿用西方说法。拜占庭文本的译本有时甚至把
译成“希腊人”。

en: Yet commitment to the Greek ethnic identification has been tepid among western historians since the late nineteenth century. They do not intend for it to legitimate arguments of ethnic Greek continuity from antiquity to the present, to buttress diachronic histories of the Greeks, or to “claim” Byzantium for the Greek nation.
is just a superficially plausible term to use instead of

, and is legitimated by western medieval sources. A recent book series called “The Edinburgh History of the Greeks” and featuring volumes of outstanding quality almost became an exception to this pattern. The series editor insists that the series will focus “on the history of a people, the Greeks, and not a place, Greece,” but the author of the Byzantine volume, Florin Curta, heads this off immediately in his introduction by making clear that his volume on the years 500–1050 ad is a history of
He correctly explains that these were Romans, and so “the Greek people” do not appear in the book.
zh: 然而自十九世纪后期以来，西方史学家认定拜占庭人为希腊族群的态度一直谈不上坚定。他们不打算用它来证明从古代到现代希腊族群连续性的论证、为跨时代的希腊人通史提供依据、或把拜占庭“认领”给希腊民族。“希腊的”只是一个表面上说得通的词，用来替代“罗马的”，并由西方中世纪史料提供正当性。一个名为“爱丁堡希腊人史”的新近丛书各卷质量出色，几乎成了这一模式的例外。丛书主编坚持丛书将聚焦“一个民族——希腊人——的历史，而不是一个地方——希腊——的历史”，但拜占庭卷的作者弗洛林·库尔塔一开篇就限定了范围，明确说明他这卷写的是公元500–1050年
的历史。他正确地解释说，这些人是罗马人，因此“希腊人民”并没有出现在书中。

en: The chief tool that modern Byzantinists have invented in order to remove Romanness from the picture, while still remaining within the Byzantines’ conceptual horizons, is to highlight Orthodox Christianity as their chief and, in some cases, their only identity. In relation to their Romanness, this works in one of two (equally arbitrary) ways. Either Romanness is denied, in the usual ways, after which we are told that the Byzantines’ “real” identity was Orthodoxy, or else the two are identified: what the Byzantines meant when they said that they were Romans was that they were Christians.
zh: 现代拜占庭学家为了把罗马性从图景中移除、同时仍留在拜占庭人的概念视域之内，所发明的主要工具，是突出正教基督教作为他们主要的、有时甚至是唯一的认同。相对于他们的罗马性，这一做法以两种（同样任意的）方式之一运作。要么按通常的方式否认罗马性，然后告诉我们拜占庭人“真正的”认同是正教；要么把两者等同：拜占庭人说自己是罗马人时，意思就是他们是基督徒。

en: Neither of these interpretations withstands scrutiny. As we will see, the Byzantines perfectly well understood the categorical difference between their ethnicity and their religion. For example, they knew that the Romans had once been pagans and they knew, especially after the conversion of Bulgaria in the ninth century, that there were Orthodox people in the world, even within their empire, who were not Romans. This was not a difficult distinction to make and it caused no confusion. The most that can be said about this interpretation is that these two identities—ethnic and religious—overlapped in Byzantium, so that in many contexts there was no reason to distinguish between them. It was between the seventh and the ninth centuries especially, when Byzantium was surrounded by non-Roman infidels, that these two identities most closely fused. We should expect them to do so. But this is not what the scholarship is getting at. It wants to sweep Romanness under the rug of Orthodoxy in order to hide it from sight.
zh: 这两种解读都经不起审视。我们将会看到，拜占庭人完全清楚自己的族群性与宗教之间的范畴区别。例如，他们知道罗马人曾经是异教徒，也知道——尤其在九世纪保加利亚皈依之后——世界上、甚至帝国内部存在不是罗马人的正教人群。这个区分不难做，也没有引起混乱。对这种解读最多只能说：这两种认同——族群的与宗教的——在拜占庭相互重叠，以至于在许多语境中没有理由区分它们。尤其在七至九世纪，当拜占庭被非罗马的异教徒包围时，这两种认同融合得最紧密。这并不出乎意料。不过，上述研究的用意并非说明两者何时重叠。它们是想用正教掩盖罗马性，让人看不见它。

en: The distinction between Roman and Orthodox identities will be discussed with reference to the sources in Chapter 2. But it had to be mentioned here, in the survey of denialism, because that is the context in which it functions. As “Roman” was taken off the table in the ninth century, and “Greek” became a problematic national category in the nineteenth, historians of the twentieth were left with nothing besides “Orthodox” to fill the gap when they have to explain to their readers who or what the “Byzantines” were.
zh: 罗马认同与正教认同的区别将在第2章依据史料讨论。这里考察否认论，也必须说到将两种认同混为一谈的用法，因为只有放在这一背景下才能理解它。当“罗马人”在九世纪已被排除在可用称谓之外、“希腊”在十九世纪成为成问题的民族范畴之后，二十世纪的史学家在必须向读者解释“拜占庭人”是谁或是什么时，除了“正教”便一无所有来填补空白。

en: By contrast, the Greekness of Byzantium remains a matter of national importance for some modern Greek historians. In addition to adopting the regular tropes of Roman denialism, they like to cite the small number of late Byzantine intellectuals who made gestures in the direction of a Greek identity, and they privilege the role of language in its definition, for what else could Greek-speakers have been if not Greeks?

But this isolates one component of a culture (language) in order to support a predetermined position. As this book will argue, however, names used for languages and ethnicity do not always overlap, and the Byzantines increasingly called their language not Greek but

or “the language of the Romans.” For us it is “Greek”; for them it was “Roman.” In time, therefore, ethnic identity overcame linguistics (the Swiss and Austrians are not Germans; the Indians and Americans are not English; and so on).
zh: 相比之下，拜占庭的希腊性对一些现代希腊史学家仍是民族大义所在。除了采纳罗马否认论的常规套路，他们还喜欢引用晚期少数朝希腊认同方向做姿态的拜占庭知识分子，并把语言的作用置于界定认同的首位，因为说希腊语的人若不是希腊人还能是什么？
但这是孤立文化的一个成分（语言）来支撑预定的立场。然而本书将论证，用于语言和族群的名称并不总是重合，拜占庭人越来越不称自己的语言为希腊语，而称为
，即“罗马人的语言”。对我们它是“希腊语”；对他们它是“罗马语”。因此随着时间推移，族群认同胜过按语言作出的归类（瑞士人和奥地利人不是德意志人；印度人和美国人不是英格兰人；如此等等）。

en: In sum, the field of Byzantine Studies suffers from an acute form of what is commonly called cognitive dissonance: while knowing that Byzantium was the Roman empire and that the Byzantines called themselves Romans, it carries on as if neither statement were “really” true. To cope with this unpleasant predicament, it has devised various evasions and terms of art by which it can confuse the issue—enough, at least, to avoid drawing obvious conclusions. These tropes are part of the catechism that Byzantinists are trained to intone in order to prove that they have mastered the subtleties of the field. And it invites the interpretation that the Byzantines were deceiving themselves in the matter of their Romanness, or attempting to deceive others, opinions that have been affirmed by otherwise serious historians. Thus, who the Byzantines were is a question that continues to defeat the field, because many of its practitioners have taken the Byzantines’ own answer off the table.
zh: 总之，拜占庭研究学科深陷通常所谓的‘认知失调’：明知拜占庭是罗马帝国、拜占庭人自称罗马人，却继续行事仿佛这两个陈述都不是“真的”。为了应付这个令人不快的困境，它发明了种种回避和术语来混淆问题——至少足以避免得出显而易见的结论。拜占庭学家受训时得熟习这套教理式的说辞；他们得念出这套说辞，以证明自己懂得本领域那些微妙之处。这样做也容易引来一种解释：拜占庭人在罗马性问题上自我欺骗，或试图欺骗他人——这些观点已被一些本来严肃的史学家肯定。于是，拜占庭人是谁这个问题继续难倒本学科，因为它的许多从业者已经预先排除了拜占庭人自己给出的答案。

en: Outside the Echo Chamber
zh: 回音室之外

en: No ideology, however pervasive, can entrap everyone all of the time. Historians of Byzantium have to work with sources that clearly and powerfully refute the fictions of denialism. Inevitably, a steady and distinguished line of Byzantinists have pushed back against its paradigm, or have made statements that do the same effectively, whether intended as a repudiation of it or not. These scholars deserve mention both for recognition and because more work needs to be done beyond what they did toward documenting, clarifying, and theorizing Byzantine Romanness, which these scholars noted and accepted but generally passed by on their way to other scholarly goals.
zh: 任何意识形态，无论多么无孔不入，都不可能永远困住所有人。拜占庭史学家必须使用那些清楚而有力地驳斥否认论虚构的史料。因此，一代代杰出的拜占庭学家不断质疑这种范式，也有人虽未必有意反驳它，提出的看法却达到了同样的效果。这些学者值得提及，既是为了表彰，也是因为要记录、澄清和理论化拜占庭罗马性，还需要在他们所做的工作之外做更多工作——这些学者注意到并接受了拜占庭罗马性，但在奔向其他学术目标的途中通常与之擦肩而过。

en: During the second half of the nineteenth century, historians transitioned from calling the eastern Roman empire “the empire of the Greeks” to calling it “Byzantium.” Honorable mention should be made of E. A. Freeman (1823–1892), who advocated the latter term as a way of avoiding the misleading ethnic term “Greek.” More than most modern historians, Freeman explained in detail how the empire was Roman, so for him “Byzantine” was just a way of saying “east Roman.”

But for most other scholars, “Byzantine” was becoming a term that avoided both ethnic Greek entanglements and the empire’s Romanness. No sooner had “Byzantium” established itself as the paradigm and name of the new field than John Bagnell Bury (1861– 1927) protested against it in the preface to his history (1899) of what he called the Later Roman Empire between 395 and 800 ad, insisting that there was no break that justified a new label. That label, he correctly foresaw, would lead to unwarranted conclusions.
Bury was the best “Byzantinist” of his generation and his narrative histories still hold up well.
By 1923, when he edited the volumes of the

devoted to the “Eastern Roman Empire,” he had come around and accepted the new label, but only as a concession to convenience. He was emphatic in the preface that, for all the cultural continuity between ancient Greece and Byzantium, the inhabitants of the “eastern” Roman empire were Romans who spoke a
version of Greek, lived in Roumelia (formerly Romanía), and were known to the Arabs as Rum. It was the western empires of Charlemagne and his descendants that had a tenuous claim to the name of Rome.
Bury knew exactly the sources of western denialism.
zh: 十九世纪下半叶，史学家从称东部罗马帝国为“希腊人的帝国”转向称它为“拜占庭”。尤其值得一提的是 E. A. 弗里曼（1823–1892），他倡导后一个术语，作为避开误导性族群术语“希腊”的方式。弗里曼比大多数现代史学家更详细地解释了帝国如何是罗马的，所以对他来说“拜占庭”只是“东罗马”的另一种说法。
但对大多数其他学者来说，“拜占庭”正在变成一个既避开希腊族群纠葛、又避开帝国罗马性的术语。“拜占庭”刚确立为新学科的范式和名称，约翰·巴格内尔·伯里（1861–1927）就在其史著（1899年）序言中抗议它——他称395至800年间的国家为后期罗马帝国——坚持不存在证明新标签正当的断裂。他正确地预见到，那个标签会导致无根据的结论。
伯里是他那一代最好的“拜占庭学家”，他的叙事史著至今仍站得住。
到1923年，当他主编《剑桥中世纪史》中关于“东部罗马帝国”的各卷时，他已转而接受这个新称谓，但只是为了使用方便。他在序言中强调，尽管古希腊与拜占庭之间存在种种文化连续性，“东部”罗马帝国的居民是罗马人，说的是一种称作
（Romaic）的希腊语，住在鲁米利亚（Roumelia，从前的罗曼尼亚），阿拉伯人称他们为鲁姆人（Rum）。对罗马之名主张薄弱的，倒是查理曼及其后裔的西方帝国。
伯里完全清楚西方否认论的根源。

en: To my knowledge, however, Bury did not explain

the Byzantines were constituted as a Roman people (i.e., by what criteria) or what this meant to them beyond pride in the continuity of imperial history. Such an exercise would probably have been beyond the analytical tools available to him at the time, and would have spoiled his excellent prose standards. Steven Runciman (1903–2000) was briefly Bury’s student and like him learned Byzantine history primarily from the sources. He was also willing to defend Byzantium against medieval biases, an instinct that would shape his later history of the crusades. In his first book, on Romanos I Lakapenos (1929), Runciman went further than Bury in trying to explain how the Byzantines were Romans. The following passage is worth quoting:
zh: 然而据我所知，伯里没解释拜占庭人
