构成一个罗马人民（即依据什么标准），也没有解释这对他们意味着什么，除了对帝国历史连续性的自豪。这样的工作大概超出了他当时可用的分析工具，而且会让他漂亮的文章失色。史蒂文·朗西曼（1903–2000）短期做过伯里的学生，和他一样主要从史料学习拜占庭史。他也愿意捍卫拜占庭、抵制中世纪偏见，这种倾向后来也影响了他书写十字军史的方式。在他的第一本书、论罗曼努斯一世·拉卡佩努斯的著作（1929年）中，朗西曼比伯里走得更远，试图解释拜占庭人如何是罗马人。下面这段话值得引用：

en: It may seem paradoxical to urge the nationality of the Empire while insisting on its cosmopolitan nature; certainly, if nationality implies a common ethnological past the Byzantines had none. But such a past is not necessary, as today the United States of America is witness; and in Byzantium the tradition inherited from the world-empire of Rome gave the Byzantines a national unity that overpowered ethnological divergencies—a national unity far more real than any that was to exist in Western Europe till the days of the Reformation. Every Byzantine citizen, were his blood Greek or Armenian or Slav, was proudly and patriotically conscious that he was Ῥωμαίος. . . . This nationality even tended to mould its people according to one fixed form; and it is as possible to talk of Byzantine characteristics as to talk of Roman and British characteristics.
zh: 一面坚持帝国具有世界主义性质，一面又说它具有民族性，乍看也许有些矛盾。诚然，如果民族性意味着不同人群有共同的族源，那么拜占庭人没有共同的族源。但这一点并非必要，今日的美利坚合众国就是明证。拜占庭从罗马世界帝国继承的传统，使拜占庭人形成了超越不同族源的民族统一。这比西欧直到宗教改革时期才出现的任何民族统一都更为真实。拜占庭的每个公民，无论是希腊人、亚美尼亚人还是斯拉夫人的血统，都怀着自豪和爱国之情，知道自己是Ῥωμαίος（罗马人）……这种民族性甚至有把人民塑成同一模样的趋势；谈论拜占庭人的特性，如同谈论罗马人或不列颠人的特性一样说得通。

en: Writing in 1929, Runciman was not able to frame the question with quite the precision that we would want, but the answer that he proposes makes perfect sense. Specifically, on the previous page he had set out to discuss the “many different races” that lived in the empire, alternating in his discussion among the terms race, nation, tribe, purity of blood, and origin. In his view, Byzantium “mixed” these “ingredients” together and produced from them a single “nation” like that of the United States. It would be a “ruinous misconception,” he urged, to deny that Byzantium had a “nationality,” which he correctly identified as that of the Romaioi, even though he evidently had trouble in defining the elements that composed it. I would also disagree with him if he meant that

inhabitants of the empire were Romaioi in this sense. As we will see, the empire contained ethnic minorities that were regarded as non-Roman by the majority and probably by themselves too. This fact explains the slippage in Runciman’s vocabulary, especially between blood and nationality. Postwar historians do not believe in Greek blood or Armenian blood (or at least they say that they do not). But for 1929, when the apparatus of the term “ethnicity” did not yet exist, Runciman’s formulation of the distinction between ethnic background and nationality is not bad.
zh: 1929年写作的朗西曼还无法以我们所希望的精确度来框定问题，但他提出的答案完全讲得通。具体而言，他在前一页着手讨论生活在帝国中的“许多不同种族”，讨论中在race（种族）、nation（民族）、tribe（部族）、血统纯正和起源等术语之间交替。在他看来，拜占庭把这些“成分”混合在一起，从中产生了一个像美国那样的单一“民族”。他力陈，否认拜占庭有“民族性”将是“毁灭性的误解”，他正确地把这种民族性认定为Romaioi（罗马人）的民族性，尽管他显然难以定义构成它的要素。如果他的意思是帝国
居民都是这个意义上的 Romaioi，我也会不同意他。我们将会看到，帝国包含在多数人看来并非罗马人的少数族群，他们自己想必也这样认为。这一事实解释了朗西曼词汇的滑动，尤其在血统与民族性之间。战后史学家不相信希腊血统或亚美尼亚血统（至少他们说自己不相信）。不过，考虑到1929年还没有围绕“族群性”一词发展出来的概念框架，朗西曼对族群背景与民族性之区分的表述不算差。

en: Not even the straitjackets of Balkan nationalism were capable of blocking the truth fully from sight, especially from scholars who spent most of their time reading the primary sources. Consider Ioannes Sykoutris, an exceptional Greek philologist (1901–1937). The formation in which the Greek people lived in the medieval period, he says, was the state of the Romans.
zh: 就连巴尔干民族主义的紧身衣也无法完全挡住真相，尤其挡不住那些大部分时间在读第一手史料的学者。想想约安尼斯·西库特里斯，这位希腊的杰出语文学家（1901–1937）。他说，中世纪希腊人生活于其中的政治实体，是罗马人的国家。

en: This [i.e., the label “Roman”] was not merely a conventional [name] or outward form. The Byzantine state was not the creation of the Greek spirit or the Greek nation. It was the continuation of this state [i.e., of the Roman empire] which was founded by the Roman people and subsequently governed by the Caesars. Its organization, army, legislation, its language (at least in the beginning), its traditions, the spiritual principle that infused it, its consciousness (for the most part), its name, its influence on neighboring peoples, etc. etc. were all Roman.
zh: 这［即“罗马”这个标签］不只是一种约定俗成的［名称］或外在形式。拜占庭国家不是希腊精神或希腊民族的创造。它是这个国家［即罗马帝国］的延续，这个国家由罗马人民建立，后来由历代恺撒统治。它的组织、军队、立法、语言（至少在起初）、传统、贯穿其中的精神原则、自我认识（大体上）、名称、对邻近民族的影响，等等，统统都是罗马的。

en: He goes on to say that all Byzantinists should have a thorough grounding in ancient Roman history and the Latin language. That might actually be one way out of this mess.
zh: 他接着说，所有拜占庭学家都应该有扎实的古罗马史和拉丁语功底。这也许真是走出这团乱麻的一条路。

en: The German historian Hans-Georg Beck (1910–1999) also devoted a part of his research to rehabilitating Byzantium as a genuinely Roman society, especially in the article
(1970) and in the long book

(1978), which is probably the best book ever written on Byzantium. Beck was not concerned with the Byzantines as a Roman ethnicity or nationality but rather with how their political society was, at core, Roman. I have presented a version of this thesis, albeit significantly modified, in a separate book, and so I will not dwell on it here.
Beck deserves mention in an honor roll of Byzantinists who took Byzantine Romanness seriously. His ideas have not had the impact that they deserved.
zh: 德国史学家汉斯-格奥尔格·贝克（1910–1999）也有一部分研究致力于为拜占庭翻案，证明它是一个真正罗马的社会，尤其在论文
（1970年）和长篇著作
（《拜占庭千年》，1978年）中，后者大概是迄今为止关于拜占庭最好的书。贝克关心的不是拜占庭人作为一个罗马族群或民族，而是他们的政治社会从根本上说是怎样一种罗马社会。我在另一本书中提出过这一论题的一个版本，尽管作了重大修改，所以这里不再赘述。
在认真对待拜占庭罗马性的拜占庭学家行列里，贝克尤其值得一提。他的思想没有产生应有的影响。

en: During the past generation individual voices have also spoken up in support of the Byzantines’ Romanness. For example, Evangelos Chrysos told the Nineteenth International Congress of Byzantine Studies (Copenhagen, 1996) that the Roman aspect was not limited to imperial ideology and the court “but had also become the point of reference in the personal field of self-consciousness of the normal citizen.” References to the Romans as a
in a great variety and large number of texts “demonstrate a sense of some sort of ‘ethnic’ identity and solidarity of all the citizens of the entire empire.”

This is entirely correct, but the problem with these programmatic statements is that they are scattered across the literature and are presented without systematic elaboration or confrontation with the distortions that pervade the field. It is thus easy for them to be lost or missed. Another interesting trend that I have noticed is that they are increasingly made by major scholars but in fields adjacent to Byzantium, for example by historians of Rus’ (Simon Franklin),
southeastern Europe (Florin Curta, who also definitely counts as a Byzantinist),
the Arabs (Hugh Kennedy),
and the medieval west (Chris Wickham, whose range is broader).

These scholars are seeing something in the sources that appears to be invisible to those trained by graduate programs in Byzantine Studies. Writing about a different set of problems, Noam Chomsky has often commented on the extraordinary expertise and mental discipline that it takes to systematically deny the obvious (e.g., that all U.S. presidents since World War II have been war criminals). We may be in a situation where professional training is providing the blinkers and blind spots that denialism requires, and that it is flourishing especially among the community of Byzantinists even as it is losing ground among outsiders.
zh: 过去一代人中，也有个别声音站出来支持拜占庭人的罗马性。例如，埃万耶洛斯·赫里索斯在第十九届国际拜占庭研究大会（哥本哈根，1996年）上说，罗马面向不限于帝国意识形态和宫廷，“而且也成为普通公民认识自身身份时的参照点”。大量多样文本中将罗马人称作一个
（genos），这“表明帝国全体公民有某种‘族群’认同和团结意识”。
这完全正确，但这些纲领性陈述的问题在于，它们散落在文献各处，提出时没有系统展开，也没有与弥漫本学科的扭曲正面交锋。因此它们很容易丢失或被错过。我注意到的另一个有趣趋势是，提出这些看法的知名学者越来越多出自拜占庭的相邻研究领域，例如研究罗斯史的西蒙·富兰克林、
研究东南欧史的弗洛林·库尔塔（他当然也算拜占庭学家）、
研究阿拉伯史的休·肯尼迪、
以及研究中世纪西方的克里斯·威克姆（其研究范围更广）。
这些学者在史料中看到了某种东西，而拜占庭研究研究生项目训练出来的人似乎看不见。诺姆·乔姆斯基在论述另一组问题时经常评论，系统地否认显而易见之事（例如二战以来所有美国总统都是战犯）需要非凡的专业知识和心智训练。我们可能正处于这样一种局面：专业训练造成了否认论赖以成立的种种视野局限，因此它在拜占庭学界格外盛行，在学界外却日渐失势。

en: Still, there are hopeful signs of change. There is a growing recognition that periodizations that erect a wall between Rome and Byzantium can cause us to miss important links and continuities.

I am also increasingly coming across acknowledgments in books from many fields, including popular books, that the Roman empire did not entirely fall in the fifth century but continued on in the east until 1453. This may be banal and trite, but it pushes back against a major pillar of a certain view of history according to which “the” Roman empire fell in the fifth century; that is, the western one, the only one that was presumably “really” Roman. Students who encounter the new paradigm are increasingly beginning to wonder in what sense the eastern empire was “Roman” too, especially when its sources, which they can now increasingly access in good translations, are chock-full of Romans. Unfortunately, Byzantinists are not well positioned to answer this question for them.
zh: 不过，仍有变化的希望迹象。越来越多的人承认，在罗马与拜占庭之间筑墙的分期会让我们错过重要的联系与连续性。

我也越来越多地在许多领域的书中——包括通俗读物——看到这样的承认：罗马帝国并没有在五世纪完全灭亡，而是在东方延续到1453年。这也许平淡老套，但它抵制了某种历史观的一大支柱，按照那种历史观，“那个”罗马帝国在五世纪灭亡了；也就是说，西部那个，大概唯一“真正”罗马的那个。接触新范式的学生越来越多地开始疑惑，东部帝国在什么意义上也是“罗马”的，尤其是他们现在能读到越来越多可靠的译本，发现东部帝国的史料里随处都是罗马人。不幸的是，拜占庭学家未能充分准备回答他们这个问题。

en: There are also signs that nonexperts are beginning to catch on that we have been bullshitting them. U.S. historian Clifton Fox wrote a paper called “What, If Anything, Is a Byzantine?,” which recognizes that “the names by which things are called are important in shaping our interpretation of reality. People are often surprised to discover that historical labels which define the past are inventions of later scholarship and ideology. . . . The people of the ‘Byzantine empire’ had no idea that they were Byzantine. They regarded themselves as the authentic continuators of the Roman world: the Romans living in Romania.”

Likewise, philosophy professor Kelley Ross has created a sprawling but lively website dedicated to the many ways in which historians have distorted the Roman nature of Byzantium, where he seeks to uncover what lay behind the smoke screen of modern labels.

It is alarming to realize that most professional Byzantinists are unable or refuse to state these basic facts in plain words, far less communicate a sense of intellectual excitement about them. Intelligent nonexperts have had to read against the grain of our scholarship in order to discover the truth.
zh: 也有迹象表明，非专家开始察觉我们一直在糊弄他们。美国史学家克利夫顿·福克斯写了一篇论文《何谓拜占庭人——如果确有拜占庭人的话？》，其中承认“事物的名称对塑造我们对现实的解释很重要。人们常常惊讶地发现，定义过去的历史标签是后世学术与意识形态的发明……‘拜占庭帝国’的人民根本不知道自己是拜占庭人。他们自视为罗马世界的真正延续者：住在罗曼尼亚的罗马人。”
同样，哲学教授凯利·罗斯建了一个庞大而生动的网站，专门讨论史学家扭曲拜占庭罗马性质的种种方式，试图揭穿现代标签烟幕背后的东西。
令人警觉的是，大多数职业拜占庭学家无法或拒绝用明白话陈述这些基本事实，更谈不上对它们传达一种智识上的兴奋感。有识见的非专家反倒得逆着我们的主流解释去读，才能发现真相。

en: Kari shrugged. “It’s like I always say,” he replied. “You Greeks are bloody clever, but you haven’t got a clue.”
zh: 卡里耸耸肩。“就像我常说的，”他答道，“你们这些希腊人聪明得要命，却什么门道都不懂。”

en: I was getting just a little tired of these Northerners’ attitude towards my people and my City. “For a start,” I said, “you can stop calling us Greeks, when we’re the great and indivisible Roman Empire, and we’ve been in business for just on a thousand years—longer, if you don’t make a distinction between the Empire and the Republic, which was founded seventeen hundred and eighty years ago—”
zh: 我对这些北方人对我们这群人和我们都城的态度已经有点厌烦了。“首先，”我说，“你们可以别再叫我们希腊人了，我们是伟大而不可分割的罗马帝国，算起来也已经开张快一千年了——如果不把帝国和共和国分开算的话，还要更久，共和国是一千七百八十年前建立的——”

en: “You can’t be Romans,” Kari interrupted. “Rome’s in Italy. And it’s hundreds of years since Rome was part of the empire. And you don’t talk Latin, you talk Greek, and none of you are Italians. In fact, most of you aren’t even Greeks any more, you’re bits and pieces of all sorts of things, all bundled up together and cross-bred, foreigners in your own City. Which is silly, if you ask me.”
zh: “你们不可能是罗马人，”卡里打断道，“罗马在意大利。而且罗马已经几百年不属于帝国了。你们不说拉丁语，你们说希腊语，你们没一个是意大利人。事实上，你们大多数甚至不再是希腊人，你们是各种来路的人搅在一起、混了血，在自己的都城里倒成了外人。要我说，这真蠢。”

en: I tried to look all dignified and aloof, but I’ve never had the knack. “Being Roman is more a state of mind than a simple accident of birth,” I said. “It’s something you aspire to. We tend to judge a man by where he’s arrived at, not where he came from.”
zh: 我想装出一副庄重超然的样子，可我从来不擅长这个。“身为罗马人，更多是出于一种心志，岂能只看碰巧生在哪里，”我说，“这是可以努力追求的。我们看一个人走到了哪里，没那么在乎他从哪里来。”

en: Franklin, “Empire of the Rhomaioi,” 518–519: “The ‘Roman’ aspect of the Byzantine self-image involves not only the political heritage of empire, but also a broader cultural identity. The Byzantines were ‘Romans’ not only by political succession, but also (as they saw it) in their culture. In its literary and rhetorical forms, in its codes of civil law, in its institutions, in its geographical, ethnographic, bureaucratic and political terminology, Byzantium expressed and described itself in terms of the ‘Roman’ past. It matters little whether or not we regard the Byzantine view of ‘Romanness’ as historically accurate or consistent; the Byzantines were, or thought themselves to be, mimetic of antiquity because they admitted no distinction or discontinuity of substance.”
zh: Franklin, “Empire of the Rhomaioi,” 518–519：“拜占庭自我形象中‘罗马’的一面，不仅涉及帝国的政治遗产，也涉及一种更广泛的文化认同。拜占庭人之所以是‘罗马人’，不仅凭借政治上的继承，还因为他们认为自己的文化也是罗马的。在其文学与修辞形式中，在其民法法典中，在其制度中，在其地理、民族志、官僚与政治术语中，拜占庭都以‘罗马’的过去来表达和描述自身。我们是否认为拜占庭人的‘罗马性’观念在历史上准确或一致，这无关紧要；拜占庭人模仿古代，或认为自己在模仿古代，因为他们不承认两者之间有任何实质上的差别或断裂。”
